**EM-6 — The beam is a chest emitter.** For the seat's BEAM the *apex* and the *reach* are measured from `controller.state.chest_sim` (= `pos_curr + CHEST_POINT[sheet][anim] (.) mirror`, `|x| <= 2` px, registry `chest_point`; PC D.12), and the *axis* is the committed `aim_angle` (1/4096 turn, `AIM_UNITS` 4096; 0 = E, counter-clockwise, spawn aim 3072 = S). Both are **reads** of `controller.state` inside `emitter.place`, never commands: aim is not an Emitter command (the kernel row's "set/toggle/aim commands" wording is refreshed in Cross-References). The tool-grip anchor `HAND_POINT` is lightless and is never read by this block, and no rule anywhere names it an origin. The beam follows *aim*, not facing: facing diverges from aim while running (PC-4 rule 3). The drawn cone and the simulated cone may diverge by up to the PC-5 accepted tolerance (≤ 2.8°, ≤ 1 tick; the Controller's `AIM_SEND_THRESHOLD` / `AIM_SETTLE_TICKS` knobs widen it to 3 ticks), which is why the agreement test (design test 1) is stated at rest. **Occlusion starts at the foot, not the chest** *(orchestrator ruling: the foot-origin rule of the technical-director over the systems-designer's sanitised walk-back, because `pos_curr` is outside every footprint by construction — `LocomotionStep` keeps the avatar's box out of them — and is free of the 2 px mirror jitter; the walk-back remains the documented alternative, ADR candidate 5)*: `CHEST_POINT.y` is -45..-25 px (`h` = −y, 25..45), so with a 24 px wall footprint the chest point stands *inside* the footprint whenever the feet are `s` px south of the first legal row in front of a north wall (`s` = 0 on that row, LY-8 b) with `h − 24 ≤ s ≤ h − 1`: the band is **1–44 px** over all animation rows (10–33 px for the walk row at `h` 34 — the first draft's "10-34" was one row's band, not the range). Walls east or west of the avatar cost at most the 4 px of chest-x offset. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The cone's apex, reach and distance are therefore measured from the chest, while the occluder segment to a subject starts at the foot origin (`pos_curr`, `beam_pose`). Other emitter kinds use their floor-plane anchor for both. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **What ships for each Lighting-spike outcome** (2D Lighting LO-10; its spike step 3b is a **pre-implementation gate for ADR candidate 5**, not a later check): outcome **B** (the light's `offset` moves the apex without moving the shadow origin) — the foot-origin rule ships as written and Lighting draws the shadow from the foot; outcome **A** (the shadow originates at the chest) with AC-57 passing — the foot-origin rule ships and the residual discrepancy (≤ 2 base px) is recorded; outcome A with AC-57 failing (a beam that renders black, or leaks through the wall, while the sim reports the opposite) — outcome **D** ships: ADR 5 adopts the walk-back (the sim occludes from the chest, walked back to the first clear point on the segment to the foot), D.4, EM-20 g and AC-10 are re-derived, and nothing else in this GDD changes. Until the spike reports, the foot-origin rule is the working rule and the worst case — a beam that renders black while the sim reports it lit, which would happen every time a player walks up to a wall — is an open risk (Open Question 5). **Near-field is aim-dependent, and the ruled answer is a drawn foot pool, not a control tax** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; ruled 2026-10-27 — user rulings: D24)*: an object between the lamp and the feet in screen-y is behind the apex when the player faces up-screen; the cone is honest about it (nothing in the drawn cone reaches it either) and the sim adds no hidden compensation. The first draft called this "a skill expression"; the systems-designer, endorsed by the creative-director, reads it as a **control tax caused by the chest-lamp decision**: an object at the player's feet, or one tile to the side, is dark in every shape in any unlit room even though it is inside Interaction's `REACH_PX` 72, and it will read as a broken prompt, not as horror. P1 is preserved if the spill is *drawn*; the price is a small loss of P3 darkness right at the body. **Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions):** `BEAM_SPILL_RADIUS_PX` ships at **24 px** (range 0–48; 0 switches the spill off) with `BEAM_SPILL_PM` 600 registered, as a dim, drawn, honest pool that gates actions only within its own actionable radius `r_lit_px` of the feet (18 px at the defaults, D.7 chain) and contributes minimally to exposure; Interaction's `REACH_PX` 72 is a different, larger distance (the hand's reach) and the spill does not light everything inside it *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; it is validated by the *dark-at-feet* metric of the first playtest (the playtest stub's placeholder decision line is 5 % of lit-beam ticks; Open Question 17). The user's chest-lamp decision stands unchanged: the lamp is still on the chest and still the only light that follows the player; the spill is a small, honest, drawn pool at the feet. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* The mechanics were fixed ahead of the ruling so that the ruling is one data value: the spill is one extra SOFT, omnidirectional, non-shadow contribution of the BEAM record, centred on the foot origin (`occ_origin`), of reach `BEAM_SPILL_RADIUS_PX` and output `BEAM_SPILL_PM` (600, range 150–1000, owner game-designer; registered), present only while the beam is on (the beam re

**EM-7 — The beam changes only on committed state.** `toggle_beam` is owned by Emitter State and fixed by the Controller (PC-5, PC-2): `actor` = the seat's beam emitter id, `actor_binding OWNED_BY_ISSUER`, `actor_source = emitter.state` (kernel CR-7: the authority check keys `(emitter.state, beam_id)`, so a beam id never matches a Body actor id or a deployable's emitter id held under another key) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*, `coalesce NONE`, `max_age_ticks` 120, origin `PLAYER`. The payload carries no state (it is a toggle: the `beam_toggle` press flips `switch_on`), so a rejected or duplicated command can never desynchronise the intent. Its apply flips `switch_on` in P2 of tick T; `emitter.place` in P3 of the same tick computes `output_pm`; the committed light therefore changes in the tick the toggle applies, with zero internal latency. The click and the hand's switch animation pre-play immediately (Presenter); **the light changes only on committed state and the Presenter never predicts beam state** (PC-5), because the beam is the human-channel anchor and may never lie, not even for one flicker. The seat's beam id is allocated by E9 inside the new-game LOADING (the Emitter's `init_world` step, or the session owner's new-game step under the same `WriteScope`, before the kernel's rebuild); the Emitter registers a **kernel binding source** at BOOTING (kernel CR-7): `beam_bindings() -> [(player_id, beam_id)]`, ascending `player_id`, a pure read of `emitter.state`; the kernel's LOADING rebuild binds each pair after every `post_restore()` (new game included), which is what lets `toggle_beam` carry `OWNED_BY_ISSUER`. The binding table is not saved (CR-7) and is rebuilt from `beam_bindings()` after every restore (EM-28). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* *Alternative considered:* the Controller allocates the beam id — rejected (CR-8). **Strobe protection is a sim guard, owned here** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; this supersedes the first-draft orchestrator ruling that routed the whole concern to the Controller's Adapter)*: the Adapter's debounce (`BEAM_TOGGLE_MIN_INTERVAL_TICKS`, owner Player Controller & Input, registry, PC-5) covers only the local human submitter, and PC-5 and Controller Open Question 18 both state that the sim-side guard "is Emitter State's to add"; with no guard here a replayed, scripted or remote submitter bypasses it and Suit SE-35's drain-sampling protection (the six-tick window) and the WCAG 2.3.1 limit rest on one client. The beam record therefore carries a canonical `last_toggle_tick` (EM-4), and `toggle_beam.validate` rejects `TOO_SOON` when `last_toggle_tick ≥ 0` and `T − last_toggle_tick < SWITCH_MIN_SPACING_TICKS` (12 commit ticks, owned by this GDD, derived in D.2b; it replaces the first draft's citation of the Adapter's `BEAM_TOGGLE_MIN_INTERVAL_TICKS` as the sim's threshold, and the Adapter constant now sits at or above it); the apply of an accepted toggle writes `last_toggle_tick = T`. *Default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20) (D32):* the same **commit-spacing rule** applies to `set_switch` for every submitter and every origin (the DOCK_STATUS glow is switched by E10, not by `set_switch`, and is exempt *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*), see below. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* The first-draft rationale ("a sim-side `COOLDOWN` would be wall-clock-shaped") was wrong: the field is counted in ticks, is canonical, and is therefore deterministic and save-equivalent. The guard applies in both directions (a turn-OFF inside the window is also `TOO_SOON`; the rule that a turn-OFF is never rejected for charge, EM-10, is about charge, not rate); `force_off` (Suit, the DEAD tick) is not a `toggle_beam` and neither reads nor writes the field. The validate order is `NO_SUCH_EMITTER`, `NOT_ACTIONABLE`, `TOO_SOON`, `CHARGE_EMPTY`. An Adapter-compliant stream is never rejected **only if** `BEAM_TOGGLE_MIN_INTERVAL_TICKS` is at least `SWITCH_MIN_SPACING_TICKS`: the Adapter's registry value is 10 today, so until the Player Controller raises it to 12 (its range 10–20 allows it; 2D Lighting Ask E-E proposes the same) a human stream pressing every 10 ticks has every second press refused `TOO_SOON` (no light change, no charge drain); this is listed under I-SPACING (D.15) and AC-90b, not hidden. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*

**Commit spacing for fixtures (`set_switch`), every submitter and origin** *(user rulings: D32; default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20). 2D Lighting Ask E-E, LO-22 assigned the guard to this GDD; no exception to "the picture never disagrees with `lit`" is granted to Lighting, whose last-resort clamp may not retime a committed switch)*: `set_switch.validate` rejects with `COOLDOWN` when `last_toggle_tick ≥ 0` and the **projected commit tick** lies fewer than `SWITCH_MIN_SPACING_TICKS` after it. The projected commit tick is the apply tick `T_a` for an OFF that would darken a lit or armed lamp, and `arm_tick` of D.2 for an ON (a deterministic function of `T_a`, EM-12). Rules: (1) an OFF applied while the lamp is still ARMING cancels an ON that never became visible and is never refused (it is not a realised transition, EM-12, AC-80); (2) the guard measures *realised switch transitions only*: a brownout, a node failure or `served_pm` falling to 0 changes `output_pm` but is the world's doing, not the submitter's, and writes nothing; (3) the guard applies to `PLAYER` and `SYSTEM` origin alike; the MVP has **two `SYSTEM` submitters in this area and neither is a `set_switch` submitter**: Attention's breach machine submits `set_beacon` (which carries no per-emitter guard, below) and Web Map & Transit switches the DOCK_STATUS glow through the guard-free mutator E10, so a refused `COOLDOWN` is only ever seen by the `PLAYER` path at the MVP (the `SYSTEM` form of `set_switch` is kept for VS-A, where a submitter receives `COOLDOWN` like anyone and may resubmit on a later tick) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; (4) a same-state `SYSTEM` `set_switch` is accepted and changes nothing (below) and is not a transition; (5) `toggle_beam` keeps its domain code `TOO_SOON` (the Controller's tests and AC-90 name it), `set_switch` uses `COOLDOWN`; both are this GDD's codes under `VALIDATION_FAILED(domain_code)`. **Consequence for the player's tap path** (stated so that no one assumes Interaction's `TAP_REARM_TICKS` 12 covers it): the tap guard spaces *submissions* by 12 ticks, while this guard spaces *commits*, and an ON commits at `arm_tick`, up to 5 ticks after its apply; so an ON tapped at tick 1201 (commit 1206) followed by an OFF tapped at 1213 (the first tap `TAP_REARM_TICKS` allows) commits at 1213, only 7 ticks after 1206, and is refused `COOLDOWN` until a tap that commits at 1218 or later (12 after 1206, subject to Interaction's own re-arm). The lamp never flickers; the refused tap changes nothing in the light, plays Interaction's failed-action cue (D.2b, delegated ruling G2) and the player taps again *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* `COOLDOWN` is a domain code, not a gameplay message (no HUD text). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* **Lighting's flash governor is never asked to delay a committed beam or fixture flip:** at 12-tick spacing any rolling half-open 60-tick window holds at most ⌈60 / 12⌉ = 5 realised transitions, which the registry `flash_count` definition counts as ⌈5 / 2⌉ = 3 flashes (a flash is a pair of opposing transitions, counted ⌈n / 2⌉, the unit ruled 2026-10-27, X9), equal to `FLASH_MAX_PER_S` 3, so the governor's defect counter (2D Lighting LO-22, Ask E-E) stays at 0 with a transition of margin (the old 10-tick floor admitted six, three flashes with none, and seven edges, four flashes, in a window closed at both ends). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* `TOO_SOON`, `NOT_ACTIONABLE` and `NO_SUCH_EMITTER` are this GDD's own domain codes under the kernel's `VALIDATION_FAILED(domain_code)` namespace. Fixture flips are now bounded here by the commit-spacing guard above (every origin), in addition to Interaction's `TAP_REARM_TICKS` (IA-21, registry, which keeps the *submission* rate) and the Graph pulse that delays every switch-ON (EM-12); `set_beacon` carries no per-emitter guard here and Attention's breach machine, its only submitter, rate-limits itself (the residual of Open Question 25). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*

| Command | Payload | Origin | `actor` / `actor_binding` | `coalesce` | `max_age_ticks` | Rejection reasons | Submitter |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `toggle_beam` | none (toggle) | `PLAYER` | the seat's beam id / `OWNED_BY_ISSUER`, `actor_source` `emitter.state` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* | `NONE` | 120 (locked, PC-5) | `CHARGE_EMPTY` (turn-ON only, from Suit's charge view), `NOT_ACTIONABLE` (`loco_state` in STAGGERED, DOWNED, DEAD — a defensive double of the Controller's input-ignore, PC-9), `NO_SUCH_EMITTER`, `TOO_SOON` (both directions: `T − last_toggle_tick < SWITCH_MIN_SPACING_TICKS`, the sim-side strobe guard) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | the Controller's Input Adapter |
| `set_switch` | `PLAYER`: `{emitter_id}`, a toggle against the true `switch_on` (as `toggle_beam`, EM-7; no believed state is carried); `SYSTEM`: `{emitter_id, on}` | `PLAYER` (an `interact`-declared verb, PC-6) or `SYSTEM` | the acting avatar / `OWNED_BY_ISSUER`, `actor_source` `body.state`, for `PLAYER`; none for `SYSTEM` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* | `NONE` (a switch is a discrete tap; the kernel's vocabulary is `NONE` / `LATEST_PER_ACTOR_PER_TICK`) | 120 (PC-2's value for action commands) | `NO_SUCH_EMITTER`, `NOT_SWITCHABLE` (kind is not FIXTURE; or **any** `set_switch` on a DOCK_STATUS fixture, whose switch belongs to Web Map's E10 `set_dock_status`, called where `pod_at` is written) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: X2)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, `COOLDOWN` (the projected commit tick lies fewer than `SWITCH_MIN_SPACING_TICKS` after `last_toggle_tick`; every origin; an OFF during ARMING is exempt; EM-7) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: D32)*, `NOT_LIVE` (**`SYSTEM` origin only**; the code keeps its name because Interaction and Attention cite it, but it means *the node is not structurally present* (defined under the table), never EM-13's output predicate 'live' *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; a `node_ref` 0 self-powered fixture has no node and is never `NOT_LIVE`; for every other fixture — Interaction IA-11(a) forbids a PLAYER-origin `validate` from reading `node().state`, `served_pm` or any health field, so a `PLAYER` `set_switch` never rejects on node state: it is accepted and flips `switch_on`, and on a structurally gone node (missing, tombstoned, dormant, `4 SALVAGED` or `5 ABSENT`) the M14 call is a no-op and the lamp stays dark by EM-13 with the switch retained, which gives the player no oracle; for `SYSTEM` origin the structural check reads `node(id).state`, never `served_pm`; a `2 FAILED` or `3 DESTROYED` node, or a dead bus with a live node, **accepts** the switch, so a player can switch a failed lamp off before it is repaired and it relights on repair only if left on, EM-13) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | Interaction's declared verb; `NOT_LIT` is Interaction's own precondition (Interaction System, designed; IA-37) |
| `set_beacon` | `{emitter_id, on}` | `SYSTEM` only | none | `NONE` | 120 (placeholder, owner technical-director, confirmed by Attention) | `NO_SUCH_EMITTER`, `NOT_BEACON`, `NOT_LIVE` (node not structurally present only, as for `set_switch`; a live node on a dead bus — `served_pm` 0 — **accepts** the command and the beacon goes STARVED and dark, EM-13; Attention E-30 expects `NOT_LIVE` for a dead bus and must be corrected) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | Attention's breach machine (designed, `attention-system.md` AT-18) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |

Same-state switches are accepted and change nothing (no dirty key); every command reaches exactly one terminal result (CR-5).

**Two predicates, two names** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: the review found one word, 'live', naming two sets. (a) **Structurally present** is the *command-validation* predicate, the only one `set_switch` and `set_beacon` `validate` may use (and, for a `PLAYER` origin, it is *not even evaluated*: Interaction IA-11(a)): the node exists in the Graph's read view, is not dormant or tombstoned, and its state is neither `4 SALVAGED` nor `5 ABSENT`. A `SYSTEM`-origin command whose node fails it is rejected `NOT_LIVE`. (b) **Live** is EM-13's *output* predicate only: structurally present **and** state not `2 FAILED` or `3 DESTROYED`; a not-live lamp has `output_pm` 0 and its record and switch are untouched. The commands are decided by (a), the light by (b). One row per node state (the AC-33 table):

| Node state at apply | `SYSTEM` `set_switch` / `set_beacon` | `PLAYER` `set_switch` | M14 `set_load_request` | `output_pm` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| missing (unknown `node_ref`), tombstoned, dormant | `NOT_LIVE` | accepted, flips `switch_on` | no-op | 0, switch retained |
| `4 SALVAGED`, `5 ABSENT` | `NOT_LIVE` | accepted, flips `switch_on` | no-op | 0, switch retained |
| `2 FAILED`, `3 DESTROYED` | accepted, flips `switch_on` | accepted | queued, as for a healthy node | 0 (STARVED) until repair, then lit if left on |
| `0 OK` / `1 DEGRADED` on a dead bus (`served_pm` 0) | accepted | accepted | queued | 0 (STARVED) until power returns |
| `0 OK` / `1 DEGRADED`, served | accepted | accepted | queued | by D.1 |


**EM-8 — Beam shape is loadout, not input; the shape table is data this GDD owns.** The four shapes (wide, narrow, split, fan) are a per-player Suit & Equipment fact set once, by the host session owner at new game through the CR-7 boot step, by `bind_beam(player_id, shape_id)` (E4). There is no "change shape" action and no Emitter command for it (PC-5), no mid-run switching and no brightness dial. The shape table below is **data owned by this GDD as the carrier of the art bible 8.3 rows** (registry: `light_shape`) so that the queried edge and the drawn edge cannot drift: Lighting's textures and cone geometry derive from it, with a build lint that the rendered reach equals the table reach ±1 px for hard-edged rows (EM-26). The art-bible columns are carried **verbatim** in degrees and tiles; the integer encodings are this GDD's derivations, tagged. Every row: *placeholder, owner art bible 8.3 / game-designer, confirmed by the Lighting spike (art bible 8.12 step 2)*. The split beam's blind spot is its identity: two cones with a dark wedge that never closes — the one shape that can never see straight ahead. That is a loadout personality, not a bug, and no one should "fix" it.

| `shape_id` | Light (art bible 8.3) | Half-angle (verbatim) | `half_angle_units` | `COS2_Q28` | Reach, tiles / px (verbatim) | Curve class | Geometry | Shadow-casting (Lighting's, informational) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 `BEAM_WIDE` | Wide cone | 30° | 341 (29.97°) | 201,441,249 | 6 / 288 | HARD | one cone | yes |
| 2 `BEAM_NARROW` | Narrow cone | 12° | 137 (12.04°) | 256,768,576 | 8 / 384 | HARD | one cone | yes |
| 3 `BEAM_SPLIT` | Split (twin) | 10° each | `SPLIT_HALF_UNITS` 114 (10.02°) each (the split row's `half_angle_units`) | 260,305,956 | 7 / 336 | HARD | two cones, axes `aim ± 206` units (18.11°; centre-to-centre 36.2°); the dark wedge is 184 units = 16.17° ≥ the art bible's 16°, and never closes | yes |
| 4 `BEAM_FAN` | Broad fan | 60° | 683 (60.03°) | 66,994,225 | 3.5 / 168 | HARD | one short wide cone ("width at the rim about 2× reach" is consistent with 60° — the chord is 1.73 R — and is carried as a placeholder) | yes |
| 5 `POOL_DEPLOYABLE` | Deployable pool (flare, torch, decoy), VS-A | 360° | — | — | 2.5 / 120 | SOFT | omnidirectional; flickers (presentation) | nearest in view only |
| 6 `POOL_GLOWSTICK` | Glowstick pool | 360° | — | — | 2 / 96 at full life (Item DB `GLOWSTICK_RADIUS_TILES`) | SOFT | omnidirectional; steady, then waning (EM-15) | none by default |
| 7 `FIXTURE` | Fixture | 360° | — | — | 3 / 144 | SOFT | static housing; never flickers (the cryo-bay gutter is Lighting's) | none (the cryo-bay lamp may take the sixth slot — Lighting's) |
| 8 `BEACON` | Alarm beacon | 20° | 228 (20.04°) | 236,913,664 | 8 / 384 | HARD | rotating sweep, 2–3 s period (EM-16) | yes |
| 9 `LANTERN` (new row) | Node lantern | 360° | — | — | 2 / 96 (`LANTERN_REACH_PX`) | SOFT | machinery-node point light | none |
| 10 `FAULT_GLOW` (new row) | Fault glow | 360° | — | — | the radius in base px of the Failure & Trail glow-table row; default 1.5 / 72 (`FAULT_GLOW_REACH_PX`) when a row carries none | SOFT | point source | none |
| 11 `BEAM_SPILL` (new row, **conditional**) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: D24)* | Foot pool of the seat's beam (the beam record's own contribution, not a separate emitter) | 360° | — | — | `BEAM_SPILL_RADIUS_PX` 24 px (0 removes the row; any non-zero value is 24–48, I-REACH) | SOFT | omnidirectional pool centred on the foot origin, present only while the beam is on, output `BEAM_SPILL_PM` 600, gates actions, non-shadow, excluded from `section_emission` (D.12) | none |

Rows 9 and 10 are new numbers (not in the art bible 8.3 table): *placeholder, owner technical-artist / Failure & Trail, confirmed by the Lighting spike*. Row 11 is new and **conditional**: it exists in the shape table iff `BEAM_SPILL_RADIUS_PX` > 0 (default 24, user ruling D24, 2026-10-27), is owned by the game-designer and art-director, and is validated by the dark-at-feet playtest metric (EM-6, Open Question 17). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* `COS2_Q28` is the square of the Q14 cosine of `half_angle_units`, in Q28 (EM-19). The split's axis is 206 units, not the 205 that 18° rounds to, because with the cones' half-angle rounded to 114 units a 205-unit axis leaves a 182-unit (15.996°) wedge and fails the art bible's "dark wedge ≥ 16°" (invariant I-WEDGE, Formulas D.15). The split's axes are ±206 units off the committed **aim**, not off facing (an art-bible wording refresh, Cross-References). The beam's `output_pm` is the constant `BEAM_BASE_PM` while on (placeholder 1000, owner game-designer; no low-charge dimming in the MVP). Reach and output of every shape row are independent of depth in the web and of Attention level: the art bible fixes the revealing radius as the one physical anchor, so "the dark presses in" is presentation (Lighting's ambient) and never a reach change (Open Question 3, resolved 2026-10-27: user ruling, kept). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*

content.content:
**EM-9 — The beam in every actionable state; DOWNED keeps it, DEAD ends it.** The beam is available while the actor is IDLE, WALK, RUN, CARRY_WALK or CHANNELLING (PC-8; the user's chest-lamp decision: nothing the hands do touches the lamp). While `loco_state == DOWNED` the beam keeps its committed state — the aim is frozen at the last committed value and the origin is the `chest_sim` of the down animation row; a downed crewmate is a locator (P1) — which is the handoff PC left to this GDD ("Emitter State decides what a downed emitter does"). While STAGGERED the state is likewise unchanged. At the tick `emitter.place` reads `loco_state == DEAD`, it forces `switch_on` false (the Controller's `DEAD` row: "beam off (Emitter State on actor death)") as an `emitter.place`-internal `force_off`, a read of `controller.state` with no command. Because Save/Load's death stub restarts from the last autosave through `request_restore` at that tick's P6, the DEAD-tick off-state is unobservable in the MVP (say so in tests). A beam that stays on over a corpse until Suit's charge runs out — a corpse as a lantern the web can see — is *not* a rule here; it is a VS-B question for Attention and Sanity (Open Questions). In IN_POD the beam follows its actor into the pod's body frame (EM-30; Ship Body's `body_of_actor` carries the frame and Web Map & Transit is designed). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*

**EM-10 — Beam charge is Suit's.** Suit & Equipment owns charge, drain, `CHARGE_EMPTY` and the HUD "beam and tool charge" reading (art bible HUD set). `toggle_beam.validate` reads Suit's charge view and rejects a turn-ON at zero charge with `CHARGE_EMPTY`; a turn-OFF is never rejected for charge (the strobe floor `TOO_SOON` of EM-7 applies to both directions). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* Suit's divisor-6 `suit.vitals` reads `emitter.state.lit` on the seat's beam to drain charge and calls `force_off(beam_id)` (E5) at zero; because `suit.vitals` runs earlier in the tick than `emitter.place`, a `force_off` takes effect in the same tick's `emitter.place`, and the owner's six-tick re-check (EM-25) then finds a channelled target unlit and aborts, so at most five ticks of channel run on a dark target. The beam is a *suit load, not a ship LOAD*: Emitter State never calls `set_load_request` for it and the Graph is not involved. (Suit & Equipment, designed: SE-8; Suit keeps the hook name `suit.vitals` and its `after: graph.propagate.atmo`.)

**EM-11 — Fixtures are switchable Graph LOADs; the lamp formula gates on the switch.** A FIXTURE carries `node_ref` (a Graph `13 LOAD` node of the LOAD subtype `LAMP` — the Item DB assigns the subtype id, currently `2 LAMP`; the Graph names only `HEATER`; provisional), `base_pm` (from the def's `emits`) and `switch_on`. Its brightness is `lamp_output_pm` (Formulas D.1): `output_pm = switch_on and armed and live ? ⌊base_pm * served_pm / 1000⌋ : 0`. The lit branch is the registry formula `power_allocation`'s output "lamp brightness = base * served_pm / 1000", reused verbatim. **`served_pm` is the tier's satisfaction `sat_k`, independent of the node's own request** (Graph D.6), so a switched-off lamp can still read `served_pm` 1000: the Emitter's own `switch_on` is the gate, not the Graph, or an off lamp would shine. Power draw is a Graph LOAD: inside the `set_switch` apply the Emitter calls M14 `set_load_request(node_ref, req_w)` with `req_w` the def's rated draw (Graph MVP: 20 W) when on and 0 when off (Class B: it clamps to `0..req_max`, queues to the next Graph phase 0, and is a no-op on an unknown, tombstoned, dormant or SALVAGED node). A lamp never renders brighter than the power it is served (Graph P1); under re-energise inrush the bank draws `req_w * INRUSH_PM / 1000` for `INRUSH_STEPS` runs, which can dim the tier-3 bank for half a second — the Graph's business, visible as an honest dip, changing no Emitter rule. The Emitter never recomputes watts and never calls M14 for node lanterns or the beam. A FIXTURE with `node_ref` 0 is *self-powered*: permitted only for the two declared subkinds, EMERGENCY (the cryo-bay emergency lamp, exactly one in the world, declared by Derelict Authoring DA-23 as `fixture_subkind_emergency`) and DOCK_STATUS (below); it has no M14 call, no ARMING and a fixed `base_pm`, and any other `node_ref` 0 fixture is refused by the authoring lint and at boot (`SELF_POWERED_LAMP_COUNT`: exactly one EMERGENCY, exactly one DOCK_STATUS per dock room, none elsewhere). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; second subkind added 2026-10-27 — user rulings: X2)* **The DOCK_STATUS fixture (user ruling X2, 2026-10-27)** keeps the pod console's lit gate satisfied at every dock without a further `act_gate` exception *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* (Interaction's IA-6 refusal of a `pod_hop` exemption stands): it is an *ordinary lit fixture* (`gates_actions` true, SOFT curve, counted in `lux_pm`, `act_lux_pm` and `section_emission`, so the web can read it like any lamp, P3 and "light is never free"), authored by Derelict Authoring on the dock room's docked-podcraft prop, in the **dock room's section** and not on the pod body (the pod section is dormant always, Web Map WM-5, and the lamp must not depend on it). It is created and discarded with its section (E1, E2), has no `node_ref` and therefore no liveness test (EM-13 concerns Graph nodes) and cannot be failed, starved or drained by any ship state, which is the point: the stranded player always finds the console lit. Its `switch_on` is driven only by the mutator **E10 `set_dock_status(section_id, on)`**, which Web Map & Transit calls in the apply that writes `p

**EM-12 — One latency story for switching.** A `set_switch` applies at P2 of tick `T_a`; its M14 call is queued to the next Graph phase 0; the lamp is **ARMING with `output_pm` 0** until `arm_tick`, the first `graph.propagate.power` run that consumed the request, and is lit on the first `emitter.place` at or after it (Formulas D.2 `switch_latency`: `arm_tick = T_a + ((GRAPH_STEP_TICKS - (T_a mod GRAPH_STEP_TICKS)) mod GRAPH_STEP_TICKS)`). Under the stated assumptions the lamp is lit between 0 and `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS - 1` ticks after the apply — at most 83 ms — and no single number from this paragraph is a design fact: D.2 derives the range with a worked example at both alignments (switch on a Graph tick; switch on the tick after one). **Assumption A1 (derived, not assumed; confirmed by the Graph 2026-10-27 in its Interactions row for this system):** kernel CR-2 ("P3 sees all of P2") and Graph LS-8 phase 0 ("apply queued unconditional inputs: `set_load_request` changes") together mean that an M14 call made in P2 of a Graph tick is consumed by that same tick's phase 0, so the range is 0..`GRAPH_STEP_TICKS - 1` ticks; the negative case, a Graph that applied only strictly later requests, would give 1..`GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` and is kept in D.2 as the labelled alternative. The direct `after: graph.propagate.failure` entry (EM-1) guarantees that the hook reads that run's output on the same tick. Switching **off** is immediate (`output_pm` 0 from the apply tick; M14 `(node_ref, 0)`); an OFF applied while the lamp is still ARMING cancels the pending ON and is not a realised transition (it writes no `last_toggle_tick`, EM-7, D.2b). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: D32)* The same "light changes only on committed state" rule PC-5 states for the beam holds for fixtures; the asymmetry (ON waits for the Graph pulse, OFF does not) is deliberate and physical: the ship has to serve the lamp, and the lamp cannot go on ahead of the ship. Fixtures never pre-play light; the wall-switch click and animation pre-play. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*

**EM-13 — Liveness: a lamp is dark when its node is dead.** A lamp or lantern is *live* iff its `node_ref` exists and `node(id).state` is neither `3 DESTROYED`, `2 FAILED`, `4 SALVAGED` nor `5 ABSENT` (Graph LS-10) and the node is not dormant or tombstoned (read each tick from the Graph read view). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: 'live' is the output rule only. Command validation uses 'structurally present' (EM-7), which excludes SALVAGED, ABSENT, dormant and tombstoned nodes but not FAILED or DESTROYED ones, so a failed lamp can still be switched.)* A not-live lamp has `output_pm` 0 while its `switch_on` stays as committed — when the node is repaired the lamp lights again without a new command. `served_pm` and node `state` are read live each tick; both change only on Graph ticks, and because `emitter.place` is `after: graph.propagate.failure` (EM-1) a Graph-tick read sees the state the run just produced, never a pre-failure-phase state. Which Graph states count as "running" for a *lantern* is the Item DB's `lantern_on_states` (default `{0 OK, 1 DEGRADED}`, resolved 2026-10-26). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(orchestrator ruling: R22 as amended at the checkpoint (CP-3) — `emitter.place` declares the direct `after:` entry, so no read is ever lagged; the technical-director's proposal to sample slow inputs once per Graph run into canonical state is not adopted, because the direct ordering needs no sampled state and a restore at a Graph tick rebuilds the identical table.)*

**EM-14 — Node lanterns are derived and switchless.** A NODE_LANTERN stands for the glow of a running machine (every machine node whose def carries an `emits` with shape `LANTERN`; the kinds are Item DB data, IDB-31, not a list in this rule: in the MVP a reactor cell, a coolant pump and a scrubber). E1 creates one NODE_LANTERN per such node, and nothing in this rule restricts the kind; the shape key stays `LANTERN` and the hue is per loop (`LANTERN_POWER`, `LANTERN_COOLANT`, `LANTERN_O2`). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* It has no switch and makes no `set_load_request` call: `output_pm` is `⌊base_pm * term / 1000⌋` when the node is live and *running* (Formulas D.3 `node_lantern_output`), where `term` is the node's `run_pm` reading. A lantern gated on `served_pm` alone would glow from a switched-off machine (the same trap as EM-11), so the lantern reads a *running* quantity `run_pm` from the Graph read view — **delivered by the Graph** (LS-19 additions, 2026-10-27: `node(id).run_pm`, 0..1000 — 0 when the requested load is 0 (LOAD `req_w` 0, PUMP `throttle_pm` 0, REACTOR `out_w` 0), otherwise `served_pm` for a consumer and `⌊1000 × out_w / out_w_rated⌋` for a REACTOR; it is not the Graph's D.9 `duty_pm`, which reads 1000 for a machine switched off on a met tier and carries the same trap as EM-11). The Emitter **consumes `run_pm` as published and clamps it** to 0..1000 (D.3): it never recomputes it from `out_w`, so a REACTOR running above rated output cannot make a lantern outshine its `base_pm`, and a rated output of 0 is the Graph's guard, not an Emitter division. There is no fallback form: a browned-out or starved machine glows at its served fraction and a lantern that cannot read `run_pm` is a boot defect, not a weaker rule (a lantern at full `base_pm` while its machine starves would lie about power state, P1). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* Lanterns are created and destroyed with their section (EM-5), counted against Lighting's lantern budget by authoring lint (EM-26), and killing the machine is the only way to dark one — "every loop you run is a lantern the web can see" (art bible Principle 3).

**EM-15 — Deployables and glowsticks: spawn on landing, steady, then waning, then gone.** `spawn_deployable(kind, pos_px, owner, life_ticks)` (E3) is called by Interaction's landing-tick hook (PC D.16: "the light exists only on landing"; the thrown light is never pre-played). The glowstick numbers are the Item DB's placeholders and are cited by name: `GLOWSTICK_LIFE_S` 150 (60–300), `GLOWSTICK_RADIUS_TILES` 2 (= 96 base px, 1.5–3), `GLOWSTICK_STACK_MAX` 4, `GLOWSTICK_WANE_FROM_PM` 400, `GLOWSTICK_WANE_FLOOR_PM` 250 (Item DB IDB-12). No tick-denominated life constant is registered by this GDD: the record's `life_total_ticks` is `ticks_for_seconds(GLOWSTICK_LIFE_S)` = 9000 taken from the def at spawn, and the Item DB's rule that **the life is counted from the throw tick, not from landing** (a stick that never lands still burns out) is honoured by Interaction passing `life_ticks` = the life remaining at landing (9000 minus `THROW_ARC_TICKS` 30 for a thrown stick). This GDD owns the curve's *semantics*, id `WANE_LINEAR_25`: while the remaining life fraction is at or above `GLOWSTICK_WANE_FROM_PM / 1000` the emitter holds its full reach (steady); below it, `reach_px` falls linearly (in the permille factor `f`, then floored to whole px) to `GLOWSTICK_WANE_FLOOR_PM / 1000` of full reach at the last tick (24 px at `life_remaining_ticks` 1); this is the Item DB's F-7 `reach_px(rem)` verbatim, so the two GDDs agree tick for tick; at `life_remaining_ticks` 0 the record is removed and its id retired (Formulas D.9). *(orchestrator ruling: the Item DB's steady-then-waning parameterisation, `GLOWSTICK_WANE_FROM_PM` 400, is adopted over the routed ruling's linear-from-spawn curve — they are the same curve at `GLOWSTICK_WANE_FROM_PM` 1000 — because the art bible specifies "steady at full value, then dimming monotonically", and the Item DB owns these numbers. A different number there is a conflict to surface, not a silent change.)* The output stays constant (`GLOWSTICK_BASE_PM`), the reveal radius shrinks, and that waning is **sim state**, not presentation, because it changes the real reveal radius (P1). It never flickers (art bible 3.2); the flicker of the VS-A flare, torch and decoy family is Lighting's and invisible to the query, which uses the steady mean. The stick lights the floor plane in ship-local px, counts as exposure like any pool (Attention may weight by area rather than radius — a pool at the floor radius has one sixteenth of the full area; the read view carries `reach_px` and the shape so either is derivable), and a stick landing in a closed room lights only that room (occluders). At most `MAX_DEPLOYABLES_LIVE` non-evicting deployables exist. **Cap eviction is a visible wane, never an instant removal** *(creative-director CD-GDD-ALIGN concern 2: a light dying with no physical cause would break the promise that a stick's waning is its only clock, and would be a P1 lie)*: a spawn over the cap (Class B never rejects; the item was already spent, and Item DB rule (c): a landed stick is spent without refund) is applied in full, and the lowest-id deployable of the same kind that is not already evicting enters an **evict-wane** — `evict_ti

**EM-16 — The beacon is a pure function of time.** A BEACON is a 20° cone (shape row 8) whose axis is `beacon_aim = (beacon_phase + beacon_dir * ⌊T * AIM_UNITS / BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS⌋) mod 4096` with `T` the kernel clock tick (non-negative modulus), `BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS` 128 (2.13 s, inside the art bible's 2–3 s; placeholder, owner art-director / audio, confirmed by the Lighting spike), so the step is exactly 32 units per tick. Direction and phase are authored data; **no per-tick angle state exists**, which is what makes save-equivalence automatic (the kernel clock is persisted by the kernel). *(orchestrator ruling: the rational form of the systems-designer over the routed ruling's `T * BEACON_UNITS_PER_TICK`, because it is identical at 128 and lets any integer sweep length be valid — the ruled range 120–180 contained exactly one divisor of 4096.)* The beacon's brightness is the lamp formula when it carries a `node_ref` (MVP: it does — a dead ship's beacon is dark, P1), switched by `set_beacon`; turned on, it starts from the angle the pure function gives at that tick (no restart at phase 0). It is a dynamic-layer emitter (it rotates) and `gates_actions` is **false** *(orchestrator ruling: the systems-designer's F9 adopted, then **ruled kept by the user 2026-10-27 (Open Question 1, D20; no longer provisional)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* — a cone sweeping over a point lights it for 14 or 15 of every 128 ticks by phase (the cone is 456 units wide and the sweep advances 32 units per tick, so ⌊456/32⌋ = 14 or ⌈456/32⌉ = 15; about 11 %), and a prompt that strobes at the sweep rate, or a channel that aborts every 128 ticks, would be the system lying about what can be worked; the beacon exposes and is seen, it does not enable verbs. This narrows the Controller's PC-6 for one kind; routed to the technical-director and game-designer)*.

**EM-17 — Fault glow is a derived emitter kind.** FAULT_GLOW emitters stand for a venting ember, a power arc and cyan O₂ mist as point sources (art bible 2.8 / Failure & Trail). They are created and removed by `emitter.place` from the Graph's failure descriptors (`failures(filter)`), each keyed by `FailureDescriptor.mode` (a failure mode 1..10, or a descriptor-only id 20..26) plus `medium`, matching the Failure & Trail glow-table keys; the MVP rows with a glow are `1/FUEL`, `1/GAS`, `2`, `3`, `7`, `9`. They use Failure & Trail's descriptor-to-glow data table (rows owned by F&T; a descriptor with no glow row creates no emitter), by comparing the Graph's list, read on Graph ticks, against the FAULT_GLOW records that already exist — no subscription (kernel CR-10) and no stored previous list. They have no switch, no Graph LOAD and no command; `output_pm` comes from the descriptor's `sev` 0..4 and the row's `sev_min` gate (D.11); they are non-shadow and count as exposure. **Position, section and frame — the anchor rule** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the first draft read mode, medium and `sev` from the descriptor but no position, and the Graph has no pixel geometry (LS-19), so the cone and radius test, the occlusion start `S`, the `section_emission` attribution and sim/render agreement had nothing to stand on)*: a FAULT_GLOW record's position is read from Layout, never guessed. For a descriptor that has a glow row: (1) `section_id` = the Graph's `section_of(descriptor.anchor)` — `section_of(node_id)` for a `(node_id, port_local_index)` anchor, `section_of(edge_id)` for an `edge_id` anchor (a compartment descriptor has no anchor and, by the F&T table, no glow row); (2) `body_id` = Layout `body_of(section_id)` (a Class 1 static query, valid straight after `restore()`, Layout LY-26 b); (3) `anchor_px` = **the first point, `base_px_polyline[0]`, of Layout's `anchor_geometry(descriptor.anchor)`** — the head of the combined wall-then-floor run, which is the source stamp the trail's glow comes from (FT-13, FT-27): a section-local base-px floor-plane point; for a `WALL_FACE` anchor it is the base of the host face, the first legal row in front of the wall (Layout LY-8 b), which already satisfies the clearance of EM-20 (b); and `origin_px` (derived) = `anchor_px + section_offset(section_id)` in the body frame, used for reach, distance and the occlusion start alike (EM-6: other kinds use their floor-plane anchor for both). `anchor_geometry` is a pure static read made once at creation and again in `post_restore`, never per tick. **Fallback when the Layout read is empty** (Layout returns nothing, without an error, only for a DISCARDED section, LY-23): no record is created on that Graph tick, `emitter_fault_glow_no_anchor` increments (release telemetry) and a debug assertion fires; reconciliation retries on the next Graph tick, and the case cannot persist for a loaded section because Layout's lint (`WALL_FITTING_NO_RUN`, AC-87) refuses a glow-capable fitting with no run. **Clearance lint, extended to every emitter anchor** (EM-20 b): a data-load lint checks the anchor of every authored FIXTURE, NODE_LANTERN and BEACON placement (the E1 inp

content.content:
**EM-18 — The illumination model: contribution, curve classes, saturating sum.** For one emitter and one subject, the contribution `c` is **0** unless all of: the subject's `body_id` equals the emitter's (EM-30), the subject is inside the emitter's radius (`d2 <= reach_px²`, a closed edge), inside its cone for cone shapes (EM-19), not blocked (EM-20). The one exception is the owner's own beam on the owner's ACTOR subject, which contributes its apex value, facing- and occlusion-independent (EM-21). For every other pair `c = ⌊output_pm * f(d, reach_px) / 1000⌋` (Formulas D.7), `d` the exact integer floor of the distance from the emitter's origin (the chest, for the beam). Two **curve classes** are carried as a data table so the Lighting spike can replace a curve without changing the API: **SOFT** (pools, fixtures, glowsticks, lanterns, fault glow) `f = 1000 * (R - d) / R`, linear to zero at the fade-out radius; **HARD** (the cones and the beacon) `f = EDGE_FLOOR_PM + (1000 - EDGE_FLOOR_PM) * (R - d) / R`, so the contribution at the rim of a full-output hard-edged emitter is `EDGE_FLOOR_PM` (placeholder 250 permille, range 160–400, owner technical-artist, confirmed by the Lighting spike) and the lit boundary **is** the drawn hard edge. *(orchestrator ruling: this is a deliberate deviation from the routed ruling's single default curve `c = output_pm * (R - d) / R`, which contradicts its own "hard outer edge exactly at `reach_px`" clause: with `LIT_ON_PM` 150 a full-output wide beam of reach 288 px would be actionable only to `d <= 244` px — 44 px, almost a full tile, inside the hard edge the player sees, the light visibly falling on a valve the hand cannot reach, which is the game lying (P1) and contradicts art bible hero #1. Three specialists converged on the edge-floor remedy; rejected: lowering `LIT_ON_PM` toward 0 (a near-black pixel becomes actionable — a different lie, and hysteresis dies) and redefining the "drawn edge" as an iso-line at 150 permille (contradicts the hard edge). Surfaced as a deviation from the ruling's default in the return value, not a registry conflict.)* The consequence is intended: a *dimmed* hard-edged emitter (output below `⌈LIT_ON_PM * 1000 / EDGE_FLOOR_PM⌉` = 600) has an honestly smaller actionable area; a full-output emitter is actionable to its last pixel (invariant I-EDGE: `BEAM_BASE_PM * EDGE_FLOOR_PM >= 1000 * LIT_ON_PM`). For SOFT classes the actionable radius `r_lit` is **the largest `d` whose integer chain (D.7) gives `c ≥ LIT_ON_PM`**, published by the sim per emitter as `r_lit_px` (the closed form ⌊R × (output_pm − LIT_ON_PM) / output_pm⌋ of the first draft ran 1 px high for some dimmed outputs and is not used) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*, inside the fade-out radius `reach_px` by design (a full fixture of reach 144 px is actionable to 122 px on approach). The **latch-release radius** `r_off_px` (the largest `d` whose chain gives `c ≥ LIT_OFF_PM`, D.7; 126 px for the same fixture) is where an already-lit subject stops being lit: Lighting draws a soft pool to the published `r_off_px` (a prompt never appears outside the visible pool), and `r_lit_px` is where an approaching subject first becomes actionable, `r_off_px − r_lit_px` px inside the drawn edge; the Lighting spike confirms the drawn edge (the art bible and Item DB "radius" numbers — 3 tiles, 2 tiles — are provisional, and the spike must decide whether they mean fade-out or readable radius). **Resolved 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix (G6): the pool is drawn to the latch-release radius (Lighting's `soft_pool_scale`, the registry source, wins); Emitter State's `lit` latch is unchanged.** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* **Aggregation is a saturating sum**, `lux_pm = min(1000, Σ c)`: integer addition is commutative, so no iteration-order dependence; several lamps in one room read brighter and expose more until fully lit. There is **no ambient term**: `AMBIENT_PM` is fixed at 0 in the sim, and Lighting's ambient is cosmetic and can never make an object actionable (P1; art bible Principle 1: unlit, not fogged). `lux_pm` sums every emitter (Horror reads it; Attention reads `emitters()` and never `lux_pm`, AT-4); `act_lux_pm` sums only the emitters whose `gates_actions` is true (EM-3) and feeds `lit` (EM-22).

**EM-19 — Cone membership is fixed-point and mirror-symmetric.** A cone test uses no trigonometry, square root or float at run time (Graph LS-1(b) precedent). Directions come from a table `DIR` of Q14 unit vectors — **the table is generated at build time by a data tool outside `src/sim/emitter/` and checked in as an integer data file, never computed in the sim module** (the boot step only loads it and asserts I-MIRROR and I-OVERFLOW, so the AC-2 lint holds) — indexed by an `AIM_UNITS` angle (0 = E, counter-clockwise, screen y down, so aim 3072 = S is `(0, +16384)`), generated from one quadrant by reflection so that `DIR[2048 - a] = (-ux, uy)` **exactly**. A subject at offset `r = anchor - origin` is in the cone iff `d2 <= R²`, `D > 0` and `D² >= d2 * COS2_Q28`, with `D = rx*ux + ry*uy` (Formulas D.5); the `D > 0` guard is required (the squared test alone accepts the opposite half-plane) and `d2 = 0` is inside every cone of that emitter, the apex included. The split beam is two tests at axes `aim ± 206` units; the wedge between them never closes (I-WEDGE), so a point is in at most one cone and its contribution is never doubled. Every product has a documented bound under 2^62 and the boot assertion refuses a build that violates it (Formulas D.15). The half-angles and the 18° offset are not integral in `AIM_UNITS`, so the shape table (EM-8) carries the encoded integers; the quantisation misplaces a rim by under 0.1° (under 0.7 px at 384 px), far inside the accepted committed-versus-drawn divergence. **The symmetry property is a test, not a hope**: the exposure of a mirrored scene (x → -x, aim `a` → `2048 - a`, `flip_h` toggled) equals the mirror image of the original exactly, for the five drawn and three mirrored facings, every `CHEST_POINT` animation row and all four shapes (Acceptance Criteria).

**EM-20 — Occlusion is integer geometry over the Layout's opaque footprints.** *(orchestrator ruling R3 — the one deliberate deviation from a routed thread's wording.)* The routed thread and the index describe occlusion as tests on "physics shapes". This GDD honours that in substance and changes the test method: the occluding shapes are the Layout's collision-footprint rectangles — walls (`WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH` 24 base px: face 72, cap 24, tile 48), closed door leaves, and props flagged `occludes_light` — which are the very rectangles the Layout `PROJECTOR` hands to physics and `LocomotionStep` already sweeps the avatar's box against (PC-14, PC-18). The query tests a segment against those rectangles in exact integer arithmetic (Formulas D.6) behind an **`OccluderSource` seam** (`rects_in(aabb)`, ascending rect id; `version(section_id)`, a monotone counter bumped when any opaque rectangle in the section changes); there is **no physics backend in the MVP**, and one may exist only as a test cross-check (the hybrid option). The reasons that decide it: kernel H10 (systems stay scene-tree free, headless) and CR-13 G3 (the 2D physics engine makes no determinism claim, so a physics-derived `lit` flowing into a persisted block would be a physics observation that must be recorded for replay); a direct-space-state query is valid only during the physics step, while the kernel allows this query from presentation prompts at render rate, exactly the unsafe site; and the 2D ray API is not sourceable in the pinned engine reference (its `physics.md` carries only a 3D example). *Rules.* (a) **Cells are unit squares, boxes are closed, and the rule is conservative** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the first draft tested the closed span of cell *indices* `[x0, x1−1]`, which treats a cell as a point, so two abutting rectangles `[0,24)` and `[24,48)` left an open strip between x 23 and x 24 and an oblique ray crossed a wall seam untouched while Lighting drew a seamless shadow — a prompt lit behind a wall, a P1 lie; every worked example used an axis-aligned ray, which hid it)*: Layout's integer coordinates name pixel cells (LY-12 b), and a cell is a unit square centred on its integer coordinate. The box D.6 tests for an occupied span `(sx0, sy0, sx1, sy1)` returned by `rects_in` (= the stored `[x0, x1) × [y0, y1)` as `(x0, y0, x1−1, y1−1)`) is the closed continuous box `[sx0 − ½, sx1 + ½] × [sy0 − ½, sy1 + ½]`, computed in **doubled coordinates** (every segment endpoint × 2) as the integer box `[2·sx0 − 1, 2·sx1 + 1] × [2·sy0 − 1, 2·sy1 + 1]` — in the stored rectangle's own terms `[2·x0 − 1, 2·x1 − 1] × [2·y0 − 1, 2·y1 − 1]`. Abutting rectangles share a box face (`[0,24)` and `[24,48)` give doubled x `[−1, 47]` and `[47, 95]`, touching at 47), so no wall seam, door-leaf/jamb joint or corner join leaves a strip; a segment that touches a box (a corner graze, an edge-on pass) is blocked; light does not leak around a corner. A segment endpoint is an integer cell, doubled to an even number against odd box bounds, so it is never exactly on a box face and is inside a box if and only if its cell is occupied. This convention is stated once, here and in D.6; Layout's occupied-span algebra (registry `rect_algebra_closed_span`, LY-12 b, D.2) remains the definition of *which cells are occupied* and of the anchor lint and is unchanged (routed to Layout: its rule text "the conservative closed test is applied to the occupied span" must read "the cell-unit box of the occupied span", Cross-References). (b) **Anchors must be at least `ANCHOR_CLEARANCE_PX` (1 base px) outside every occluding rectangle** (Chebyshev distance in cells from the occupied span, Layout D.2: a wall stored [408,432), whose occupied span is x 408..431, admits anchors at x = 407 and x = 432 and rejects 408 through 431; registry: `rect_algebra_closed_span`, the Layout's half-open convention), checked by authoring lint at registration. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **What the clearance means under the unit-square convention:** at 1 the anchor's centre is half a pixel (one doubled unit) outside the occluding box face, with its own cell directly adjacent to the wall, which guarantees that the segment's start is outside every box; a clearance of 0 would put the anchor inside the box. The check covers **every emitter anchor, not only subject anchors**: fixture, lantern and beacon placements at instantiate (a data-load lint) and FAULT_GLOW anchors at creation (EM-17); an emitter anchored on its own wall footprint would light nothing in its room and, in the first draft, raised no diagnostic. An anchor found strictly inside a footprint at run time is treated as blocked from every emitter (fails safe to dark) and increments `emitter_anchor_clearance_fail`. (c) **Actors and horrors never occlude.** A shadow with no occluder is a stage-2 sanity symptom (art bible 3.2 open item: it should not cast an occluding shadow) and must stay an unambiguous tell; so a horror standing in a beam leaves the beam unchanged and the subject beyond it lit. (d) **Door state is read from the Layout projection of the Graph's `door_state`** (Graph LS-6: the Graph owns door state and opening `area`) — the same door-leaf rectangle `collide` uses (PC-3, PC-18 test 7: same-tick door response) — so there is one source for collision and light, derived from the Graph in the same tick, and Emitter State holds **no door flag**. The door-leaf rectangle is the Layout's `door_leaf_gap` projection (Layout D.5, LY-9): `leaf_w` is continuous in the Graph's opening area and `leaf_w` 0 yields no rectangle, so no open-fraction threshold exists; `DOOR_LIGHT_OPEN_PM` is deprecated and unused. (e) A door interactable registers **two** face subjects, one per face, each `ANCHOR_CLEARANCE_PX` outside the leaf, so a closed leaf blocks the other side's emitters from each face subject (Interaction's registration; EM-21). (f) No glass or translucent occluders in the MVP. (g) The occlusion segment starts at the occlusion origin of EM-6 (the foot, for the beam). The wording this implies for the index and the kernel is routed in Cross-References. *Alternatives considered:* a physics-space query against a dedicated occluder layer — rejected (above); reusing a rendering occluder object as the sim's occluder — rejected outright, it is Lighting's rendering object and the sim never reads it.
