content.content:
**EM-21 — Subjects register; each has one anchor; an unregistered ref answers like an unlit one.** Anything that asks "am I lit" registers a **subject** with `register_subject(ref, kind, anchor_px, section_id)` (E6) and withdraws it with `unregister_subject(ref)` (E7). Subject kinds: OBJECT (an interaction anchor), ACTOR (the foot origin, *read* from `body.state` each tick, not supplied; its `section_id` and `body_id` are read the same way from Body's `actor_section(actor_id)` and `body_of_actor(actor_id)`, BDY-29, so the owner's exposure is attributed to the section the foot stands in and moves with it across a door), HORROR, ITEM (loose items). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The subject's single `anchor_px` is the only sampled point: a large object half in a beam is lit iff its anchor is (the same one-point model as `REACH_PX` and focus scoring, PC-6, and the cheapest symmetric one). Sections are never point-sampled; they aggregate by emitter list (`section_emission`, EM-27). `moving` is a per-registration flag: ACTOR and HORROR subjects are always moving; an ITEM registers static (a carried item is unregistered at pickup and re-registered at drop); only moving registrations count against `MAX_MOVING_SUBJECTS`. **The owner stands in their own light** *(orchestrator ruling: the systems-designer's SD-7 adopted with the checkpoint fix CP-9 — as first proposed it excluded the owner's beam from the owner's lux, so a player alone with the lamp on would have read `lux` 0 to Horror, the opposite of P3)*: the owner's own beam contributes its **full `output_pm`** — the d = 0 apex value, which EM-19 already places inside every cone — to the owner's ACTOR `lux_pm`, independent of facing and of occlusion, so the owner's self-lux never flips with the way they face; it is not added to the owner's `act_lux_pm` (the player is never the target of their own verb for the `act_gate` lit test; the one self-targeted verb, the ACTOR_SELF self-patch, is `act_gate`-exempt, Interaction IA-6, so `lit(ACTOR_SELF)` is never consulted for it and no self-lit or anchor-coverage rule is owed here; crediting the owner's beam to `act_lux_pm` is deliberately not done) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. Attention reads the beam as *emission* (`emitters()`, `section_emission`) and does not add the same beam again to the owner's lux (EM-27). Every other beam lights the owner, and the owner's beam lights everyone else, by the ordinary cone test. **An unregistered ref answers exactly like an unlit registered one** *(orchestrator ruling: SD-16 adopted — a P4 requirement)*: `lux(ref)` is 0 and `lit(ref)` is false in release builds, so the Perception Filter's phantom targets (kernel Open Question 14) cost Interaction the same check as real unlit ones and the query cannot become an existence oracle that undermines the phantom-loot hallucination. A debug-only `registered(ref)` exists for tests and the Debug Overlay. Registration over `MAX_EXPOSURE_SUBJECTS` returns false, increments `emitter_subjects_overflow` and the subject reads dark (fails safe); a duplicate registration is a no-op returning false. **Runtime overflow is a content or budget defect, never a gameplay state** *(creative-director CD-GDD-ALIGN concern 3)*: failing safe to dark is the right behaviour for a subject the table cannot hold, but a real object sitting visibly inside a beam that refuses to prompt breaks design test 1 (the honest edge) and the P4 "reach for it" falsifier, because the player reads a real lit object as a hallucination. So the caps are held upstream by budgets, not discovered at run time (EM-24, D.15 I-CAPS (d)), and the two counters `emitter_subjects_overflow` and `emitter_moving_overflow` ship in release builds as telemetry (the probe counter went with the probes, EM-24) (a counter in the diagnostics block, not only a debug assertion), so a budget breach in a playtest or live build is visible and reportable. The subject table fields are below; every subject's `body_id` is derived (Layout `body_of(section_id)`; Body `body_of_actor` for an ACTOR) and never stored or hashed *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. Registrations are canonical (EM-28, R16): registrants (Interaction, Horror, Suit) own the thing registered and re-register idempotently in their own `post_restore`, which `restore_after` `emitter.state` allows.

| Field | Type | C / D | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ref` | kind-tagged integer | C | opaque to this block |
| `kind` | enum | C | OBJECT, ACTOR, HORROR, ITEM |
| `anchor_px` | int2 | C | OBJECT and ITEM: **section-local** (Layout's frame, as Layout's `subject_anchors` returns it), composed with `section_offset(section_id)` at evaluation like an emitter's, so a weld or detach moves nothing; ACTOR: read from Body in the body frame; HORROR: the body-frame position Horror passes through E6 / E8 (Horror HE-34), in the record's current body frame; a weld or cut that changes the `section_offset` of the horror's section shifts that frame, and Horror re-bases its stored body-frame points and re-sends E8 in its next run (Horror HE-22 as amended 2026-10-28); until E8 lands the subject reads from its last anchor, the same one-run lag the E8 row accepts *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. The frame each registrant passes is to be confirmed by Interaction and Horror (Open Question 29) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| `section_id` | u32 | C (OBJECT, HORROR, ITEM); **D for ACTOR** | the section; an ACTOR's is rewritten every tick in W0 from Body's `actor_section` (derived, never hashed); when `actor_section` answers NONE (a defect-only state, BDY-29) the previous value is kept and `emitter_actor_section_none` increments *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| `body_id` | u32 | **D for EVERY subject kind** | OBJECT, ITEM and HORROR: Layout `body_of(section_id)`, re-read as for emitters (EM-4, EM-23 W0); ACTOR: Body `body_of_actor` rewritten every tick in W0 (the NONE rule above is unchanged). Never hashed. HORROR: the registered `section_id` is Horror's at E6; a HORROR whose section leaves its body (a cut) is Horror's to re-register or send to TRANSIT (Horror HE-22 / AC-HE-48 already re-derive `body_id`); the Emitter never guesses a moved horror's section *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* |
| `moving` | bool | C | |
| `static_lux_pm`, `static_version` | int | D | the cached static-layer partial sum and the version it was built at |
| `lux_pm`, `act_lux_pm` | int 0..1000 | D | |
| `lit` | bool | C | the hysteresis bit (EM-22): canonical, one bit per subject, snapshotted and hashed |
| `top_emitter_id` | u32 | D | |
| `last_eval_tick` | int | D | |

**EM-22 — `lit(subject)`: threshold, hysteresis and the beacon exception.** `lit(ref)` is a hysteresis filter over `act_lux_pm` (Formulas D.8): it becomes true when `act_lux_pm >= LIT_ON_PM`, becomes false when `act_lux_pm < LIT_OFF_PM`, and holds between. Placeholders `LIT_ON_PM` 150 (range 100–300) and `LIT_OFF_PM` 120 (60–140), the `LIT_THRESHOLD_PM` family **owned by the technical-artist** (art bible 7.0: "the illumination threshold that enables prompt and inspect-card drawing"), confirmed against the rendered edge in the Lighting spike (8.12 step 2). A newly registered subject starts unlit and is evaluated at the next `emitter.place`. A hard-edged rim is a *step* (a full-output rim contributes `EDGE_FLOOR_PM` then 0 across one pixel), which the 150/120 hysteresis never sees; rim chatter while a beam sweeps is held by the Controller's committed-aim quantisation (`AIM_SEND_THRESHOLD` 32 units) and `FOCUS_STICKY_MARGIN` (PC-6), and the hysteresis bites only for dimmed or soft light (brownout, waning glowsticks, fixture pools). There is **no dwell** (`LIT_OFF_DWELL_TICKS` fixed at 0): keeping `lit` true after the light went would be a window where the sim says lit and the world is dark, a P1 lie. `lit(ref)` and `lux(ref)` are separate answers because the beacon's sweep must not strobe prompts (EM-16). **The hysteresis bit is canonical** (checkpoint ruling CP-2): `lit(ref)` depends on last tick's answer, and a subject whose `act_lux_pm` sits between `LIT_OFF_PM` and `LIT_ON_PM` has no other source for its bit, so by EM-4's own definition the bit is a discrete fact — one bit per registered subject, at most `MAX_EXPOSURE_SUBJECTS` bits, snapshotted and hashed. `post_restore` rebuilds `lux_pm`, `act_lux_pm` and `top_emitter_id` from the restored emitters and **keeps the bit**; the next `emitter.place` applies hysteresis normally. A subject saved at 130 permille and lit is therefore lit after the restore, and Interaction's `validate` at T+1 reads the same answer in the live run and the restored run (kernel G4). *(orchestrator ruling: the systems-designer's canonical bitset is the rule. Rejected alternative: rebuild every bit against `LIT_ON_PM` in `post_restore` (the earlier ruling R6) — a subject between the thresholds would flip from lit to unlit across a restore, `validate` at T+1 would accept in one run and reject `NOT_LIT` in the other, and canonical state downstream would diverge.)* Interaction's `validate` and the HUD prompt call this same `lit(ref)`, so the prompt never lies by omission (PC-6).

**EM-23 — The order of work inside `emitter.place`; static and dynamic layers; no subscriptions.** The hook does, in this order and nothing else: **W0** read upstream (`controller.state` and `body.state` for bound seats; the Layout `OccluderSource.version(section_id)`; the Graph's `served_pm` and `node(id)`; on Graph ticks the Graph's `failures(filter)`), and rewrite the derived `section_id` and `body_id` of each BEAM record and ACTOR subject from Body's `actor_section(actor_id)` and `body_of_actor(actor_id)` (a tick in which the foot crosses a door moves the beam's section in that tick) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*, AND, for every loaded section whose Layout `static_version(section_id)` differs from the value cached at the last W0 (a derived per-section cache, never hashed, reset in `post_restore` so the first W0 after a restore re-reads everything), re-read `body_of(section_id)` and `section_offset(section_id)` and rewrite the derived `body_id` of every record and non-ACTOR subject whose `section_id` is that section (cost `W_FRAME` each, D.14); a change of `body_id` or `section_offset` is a FRAME CHANGE of that section *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; **W1** lifecycle (DEAD force-off, deployable aging, evict-wane (D.9b) and removal, `arm_tick` arming, fault-glow reconciliation); **W2** derive every emitter in ascending id (origin, aim, reach, `output_pm`, record `lit`); **W3** find the static-layer rows whose inputs changed; **W4** update them by deltas, in ascending (emitter id, subject ref), **synchronously — nothing is left pending past W4** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; **W5** the dynamic layer for every subject (with the owner-beam special case of EM-21: the owner's own beam adds its apex value to the owner's ACTOR `lux_pm` with no cone or occlusion test); **W6** saturating sums, hysteresis, write the subject table, record the tick's counted work; **W7** write dirty keys (EM-26). The **static layer** (FIXTURE, NODE_LANTERN, FAULT_GLOW, resting DEPLOYABLE) is cached as **per-pair contribution rows** `(emitter id, subject ref) → {d, f_pm, c}` (a row exists only while the emitter is in radius and unblocked) plus, per subject, an **unsaturated** raw sum `Σ c`, clamped to 1000 only when the answer is read. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The first draft cached a saturated partial sum, which is exact for *adding* an emitter (`min(1000, min(1000, a) + b) = min(1000, a + b)`) but cannot *remove* one (a saturated 1000 has forgotten what it summed), so every output change would have forced a full re-evaluation of the subject; with the pair rows every change is a delta: (i) an emitter's **output** changes (to or from 0, a brownout step, inrush): `c = ⌊output_pm × f_pm / 1000⌋` is recomputed from the stored `f_pm` with no geometry, and an `output_pm` of 0 stores `c` = 0 with no multiply while the rows (the geometry) are kept, so a blackout is a zeroing of rows and not a re-evaluation of the ship, and switching back on is a delta too; (ii) an emitter's integer **reach** changes (a waning stick): `d` and `f_pm` are recomputed for its rows and rows beyond the new reach are dropped, with no occlusion test (reach only shrinks, so no pair is added); (iii) an emitter is **created** (its candidate subjects are tested radius first, then occlusion, and rows are added) or **removed** (its rows are dropped); (iv) a subject is **registered or moved** (it is tested against the static emitters in range); (v) an **occluder** changes (only pairs whose segment bounding box meets the changed region are re-tested, below); (vi) the layer is **cold** (`post_restore`, section instantiate: everything is built); (vii) a **FRAME CHANGE** (a weld or cut, Layout LY-16 / LY-17) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. Rows store `d`, `f_pm` and `c` and no coordinates, and a weld or cut moves a whole body by one translation (`rot_q` is 0 in the MVP, Layout D.6 / D.12), so: (a) rows whose emitter and subject lie in the same moved component are KEPT unchanged; (b) rows whose emitter `body_id` differs from the subject `body_id` after re-derivation are DROPPED (a cut: the rows that crossed the severed seam; cost `W_DELTA` each); (c) every subject with a changed `body_id` or on the host side of the seam is tested radius-first against the emitters of the OTHER side that are now on its body, and rows are ADDED (a weld; cost `U_sub` with the cross-seam counts of S8); (d) for each socket-host section the hatch slot set changed (PLATE <-> JAMB + LEAF), so pairs whose segment bounding box meets the changed region are re-tested exactly as for a leaf change (narrowing rule L / D). Layout reports the kind of change per section as `changed_region(section_id)` = ALL, REGION(box) or FRAME: FRAME = translation only, no re-test; REGION = the socket slot union box (a socket-host section that also moves reports REGION, and the Emitter detects its translation by comparing `section_offset(section_id)` with its cached value); ALL (build, discard, restore, or attach / detach if Layout declines REGION / FRAME) = cold rebuild of the affected bodies, priced as S8b. The rebuild stays synchronous (W3 / W4); nothing is pending past W4. Rows are derived, never hashed, rebuilt in ascending (emitter id, subject ref), and sized by ADR candidate 4; a row-table overflow changes cost, never an answer, and increments `emitter_pair_rows_overflow`; the **dynamic layer** (BEAM, BEACON, which rotate or translate every tick) is recomputed per tick with the cheapest rejects first — radius, then cone, then the occlusion test. A subject's static rows are updated when `emitter.place` *observes* a change in what it read last tick: the section's `OccluderSource.version(...)` changed, an emitter's `output_pm` or integer `reach_px` changed, an emitter was created or removed, or the subject moved. **Never by subscription**: kernel CR-10 ("simulation systems never subscribe; sim-to-sim is ordered step reads or commands"); dirty keys are the notification channel for PRESENTATION and friends, not an input to this block. A pose-unchanged skip (a dynamic emitter whose origin, aim, output, shape and occlusion origin equal last tick's skips re-evaluation) is a pure optimisation and changes no answer. A static emitter's cost is paid when something changes, not every tick; a glowstick's reach steps by one px every 50 ticks while it wanes (3600 ticks over 72 px, D.9), so the rows of the subjects in its range are recomputed that often (D.14, S5). **Narrowing rule for door leaves** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: `OccluderSource.version(section_id)` says only *that* something in the section changed, and a leaf bump arrives at the Graph's step rate while a door travels (roughly ten per second), so a response that re-tests every pair of the section would cost 11,522 units per bump (D.14, S1: 14 × `T_sub` 823) against `B` 10,000 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. The Emitter therefore re-tests only pairs whose segment bounding box meets the changed region: **(L)** Layout publishes the changed region with the bump (ask E-N, a union box of the old and new leaf rectangles; a structural bump — build, discard, restore — reports `ALL`; attach and detach report REGION / FRAME (trigger vii) when Layout supplies them, else `ALL`), or, if Layout declines, **(D)** every pair whose segment bounding box meets a door-leaf pre-filter box of its section is tagged *dynamic* and evaluated every tick in the dynamic layer, which costs the same amount every tick instead of once per bump (priced in S1). ADR candidate 4 chooses between L and D on Layout's answer; both fit the budget. A restore-time bump (Layout's `post_restore`, version 1 to 2) is treated as a leaf-region change over that section's leaf boxes, not as `ALL`, because structural geometry is valid straight after `restore()` (Layout LY-26 b). **The contract is "never stale", and the rebuild is synchronous** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; resolves the question that D.13's age bound left open)*: W3 and W4 finish every update inside the tick, before W6 writes the table, so there is no pending state and the D.13 bound (age 0 or 1 tick) holds for every reader, including Interaction's `validate` at T−1 and its six-tick re-check, Attention and Horror. A tick whose updates exceed the ceiling of D.14 still completes them, increments `emitter_rebuild_over_ceiling` and is a hitch to be removed by content or by the ordered fallbacks, never deferred. **Alternative (b), rejected and recorded for ADR candidate 4:** a deterministic counted-unit cap per tick, a widened staleness bound and a fail-safe lit-or-dark rule for pending subjects. It was rejected because (1) `lit` would then depend on a rebuild queue that is derived, not canonical, so a snapshot restored mid-queue (which rebuilds cold and complete) would answer differently from the uninterrupted run — kernel G4 broken in exactly the way the old probe budget broke it (EM-24); (2) a fail-safe-dark rule would blink the prompts of a whole room on every door bump; and (3) it would rewrite the age bound that three designed GDDs already build on. The ceiling's named owner is the technical-director; the exposure spike reports it (AC-53).

**EM-24 — Counted work, not wall-clock; the caps.** The per-tick exposure cost is bounded by **counted work units**, never by timing — a time-based governor would be nondeterministic. The caps (all *placeholder, owner technical-director, confirmed by the exposure spike and the Interaction / Derelict Authoring content counts*; never inherited from a default of 64): `MAX_EXPOSURE_SUBJECTS` 192 (derived from the MVP slice's 14 compartments — home-ship 5, derelict A 4, derelict B 5 — their verb-bearing nodes, doors counted twice for their two face subjects, loose items, actors and horror subjects; Formulas D.14; *orchestrator pick: the systems-designer's 192 over the technical-director's 128, because doors register two subjects (EM-20 e) and the MVP Graph's node count supports a larger interactable set*), `MAX_MOVING_SUBJECTS` 16 (the 17th moving registration returns false, increments `emitter_moving_overflow` and the subject reads dark, the same fail-safe as `MAX_EXPOSURE_SUBJECTS`), `MAX_EMITTERS` 96, `MAX_DEPLOYABLES_LIVE` 8, `MAX_DEPLOYABLES_EVICTING` 4, `MAX_FAULT_GLOW` 10. **The caps are content budgets, held at data load, not gameplay states** *(CD-GDD-ALIGN concerns 1 and 3)*: the MVP slice has exactly 8 live faults world-wide, of which a welded body carries at most 6 simultaneous glow rows (registry `mvp_fault_allocation`); I-CAPS therefore requires `MAX_FAULT_GLOW` to be at least the most simultaneous glowing authored faults on one body plus 25 % (⌈1.25 × 6⌉ = 8; the cap of 10 keeps 2 of headroom), and requires the **dynamic registrants** that arrive after boot to be held to per-category budgets owned by their authors: Derelict Authoring owns the budget for authored OBJECT and ITEM subjects and for dropped loot and spawned salvage per section, Horror Entities owns the horror-subject budget (`HORROR_SUBJECTS_MAX` 2 (Horror Entities, registry), all moving; Horror's `horror_subject_count` holds `HORROR_SUBJECTS_MAX` + `A_max` 4 = 6 ≤ `MAX_MOVING_SUBJECTS`) and the share of `MAX_MOVING_SUBJECTS` it may use, Interaction owns the dropped-item registrations, and the deployable budget is `MAX_DEPLOYABLES_LIVE` + `MAX_DEPLOYABLES_EVICTING` (D.14, D.15 I-CAPS (d)). A runtime overflow of any cap is a defect of one of those budgets, is counted by a release-build telemetry counter (`emitter_subjects_overflow`, `emitter_moving_overflow`, `emitter_fault_glow_overcap`, `emitter_fault_glow_evictions`, `emitter_deployable_evictions`, `emitter_deployable_evict_overflow`, and, added by the 2026-10-27 design review, `emitter_create_refused`, `emitter_fault_glow_no_anchor`, `emitter_anchor_clearance_fail`, `emitter_reach_invalid`, `emitter_actor_section_none`, `emitter_pair_rows_overflow`, `emitter_rebuild_over_ceiling`, and, added by the re-review, `emitter_dock_status_missing`, `emitter_invalid_transition` and the playtest counters of the metric stub) as well as asserted in debug, and is never something a design relies on. `EXPOSURE_BUDGET_MS` is **0.4 ms P99** for `emitter.place` plus all exposure evaluation (placeholder, spike on the release export on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK, delegated ruling R12; the kernel's `STEP_BUDGET_MS` 4 is a logging threshold and P3's target is ≤ 2.0 ms P99 with the Graph at 0.5 ms and Controller + Body about 0.3 ms). It is the *steady-state* budget; the named rare-event scenarios of D.14 are held to `EXPOSURE_TICK_CEILING_MS` (hot class) and `COLD_REBUILD_CEILING_MS` (cold class), both owned by the technical-director. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* Mandatory work (the dynamic layer, static rebuilds, the subject table) is never skipped. **Creation at `MAX_EMITTERS`** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the first draft had no run-time rule at the global cap)*: when the record count equals `MAX_EMITTERS` a creation is **refused**, never made by removing a light that has a physical cause. E1 refuses the section's remaining records, `spawn_deployable` returns false (the item was already spent, Item DB rule (c)), and a FAULT_GLOW reconciliation creates nothing for the lowest-ranked descriptors; each refusal increments `emitter_create_refused` (release telemetry, per kind) and asserts in debug. Within one pass creations are admitted in `priority` order, highest first (BEAM 255, BEACON 200, FIXTURE 120, DEPLOYABLE 100, FAULT_GLOW 80, NODE_LANTERN 60; ties by ascending creation order), so the light the player most needs is the one kept; the seat beams are never refused, because their slots are reserved (I-CAPS (a) counts the bound seats). The cap is a content budget held by I-CAPS (a); the rule exists so that a breach is deterministic, counted and visible, never a gameplay state. **Probes and `lit_by(point)` are deferred to Vertical Slice A** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: no MVP consumer calls them (Horror HE-19 and HE-25 use Layout `room_at` / `room_adjacency` and make no `probe()` call, Attention AT-4 makes none, Sanity no longer uses `lit_static` (deferred to VS-A, EM-25), and Interaction's re-checks are `lit(ref)` lookups), so `probe`, `lit_by`, `MAX_PROBES_PER_TICK`, `W_PROBE`, `probes_allowed` and the probe counter are removed from the MVP read view, budget and acceptance criteria. The first draft derived `probes_allowed` from the previous tick's counted work `T_mand_prev`, which depends on cache hits and skips, is not canonical (absent from EM-28) and is rebuilt differently after `post_restore`, so the same probe could answer OK in a live run and `UNKNOWN` after a restore — a kernel G4 break that the old AC-54 could not detect. **Reserved for VS-A:** if probes return, their budget is a *constant* number per tick that is never derived from counted work, and their signatures take the frame, `probe(body_id, point)` and `lit_by(body_id, point)`, because geometry is compared only within one body (EM-30). The GDScript op cost is not sourceable from the pinned engine reference (no scripting module), so every cost number is a model parameter for the spike; the fallback if the dynamic layer is too slow is a baked per-room illumination grid for the static layer (the brief's option c), then reducing `MAX_MOVING_SUBJECTS`, then room-gated broadphase (the numeric decision table of D.14 governs the order). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*

**EM-25 — Query semantics, the read view and the staleness bound.** Public reads are table lookups against the subject table and the emitter records; they are pure, side-effect free and callable from `validate`, from P3 and from presentation prompts, **never from notification handlers that decide state** (kernel C.3 row 7). Because `emitter.place` runs every tick, a reader that does not declare `after: [emitter.place]` sees a value **at most one tick old**; P2 `validate` sees the table committed by tick T-1's `emitter.place`; a hook that declares `after: [emitter.place]` sees the current tick (the routed ruling's correction of the brief's "up to 5 ticks", which was borrowed from the Graph's divisor-6 caveat and does not apply to a divisor-1 hook). Source ages stack on top and are named, not hidden: the beam's committed aim is up to the Controller's tolerance behind the drawn aim; a lamp's brightness follows `served_pm`, which changes only on Graph ticks. Owners of channelled verbs re-check exposure every 6 ticks through the same `lit(ref)` and abort if unlit at a check (PC-7); a single-tick flicker between checks is tolerated. Attention declares `after: [graph.propagate.power, emitter.place]` (cross-divisor `after:` is already in use: `controller.step` is `after: suit.vitals`) and Horror Entities declares `after` both Attention and `emitter.place` (kernel row 9; HE-3), so the former asks are met and AC-60 lints them. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*

| Read-view entry point | Returns | Staleness |
|---|---|---|
| `emitters(filter)` / `emitter(id)` | records, ascending id, with derived fields, stamped with the monotone `tick` of the committed table. **The read is served from a per-tick snapshot built once in W7** (typed or packed columns; emitter ids and subject refs held in sorted columns, so iteration is ascending id by construction and never by Dictionary insertion order, which is not ascending after a restore; the storage layout is ADR candidate 6) and returns a read-only view or fills a caller-provided buffer (2D Lighting E-F). **No-retain rule:** a reader may not keep the view, a slice of it or a reference into it beyond the call that obtained it — the snapshot is overwritten in W7 of the next tick — and the lint forbids storing it in a field. A GDScript read that cannot meet "copy-free, read-only, no allocation" as plain `Dictionary` code is why the layout is an ADR and not an implementation choice *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | current if `after: emitter.place`, else ≤ 1 tick |
| `beam_of(player_id)` | the seat's beam id | exact |
| `beam_bindings()` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* | `[(player_id, beam_id)]`, ascending `player_id`: the kernel binding source registered at BOOTING (kernel CR-7); a pure read of `emitter.state`, so the kernel's LOADING rebuild can bind the seat beams after every `post_restore()` | exact |
| `beam_spill(beam_id)` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | the foot spill's derived record while the beam is on and `BEAM_SPILL_RADIUS_PX` > 0, else null: `{beam_id, kind BEAM, shape_id 11, origin_px (foot origin), reach_px, r_lit_px, r_off_px, curve_class SOFT, output_pm, hue_class, section_id, body_id, priority}` (EM-26) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. Not a stored emitter, not in `emitters()`, not in `section_emission`; the no-retain rule applies as for `emitters()` | as `emitters()` (the committed table) |
| `lux(ref)` / `lit(ref)` / `top_emitter(ref)` | `lux_pm` 0..1000 / bool / emitter id (unregistered ref: 0 / false / none) | as above |
| `lit_by(body_id, point)` / `probe(body_id, point)` | **not in the MVP read view — deferred to Vertical Slice A** (EM-24). The names are reserved; a call in MVP source is a lint error. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | — |
| `section_emission(section_id)` | integer (D.12), read from a **precomputed per-section array built in W7** (O(1) per call; the first draft summed over all emitters per call, O(E)) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | as above |
| `subject_headroom()` | `MAX_EXPOSURE_SUBJECTS` − registered subjects (int ≥ 0); Interaction's `drop` / `place_loose` need it above 0 | as above |
| `emitters_near(body_id, px, r)` (name provisional) | ids of emitters on `body_id` whose origin lies within `r` px of `px` (inclusive, `d²` ≤ `r²`), ascending id; a filter of the records, not a probe (Horror HE-35 L3 disturbance, C-HE-15) | as above *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| `lit_static(ref)` **— deferred to VS-A; not in the MVP read view** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | bool: the subject's static-layer `lux_pm` alone (fixtures, node lanterns, fault glow, resting deployables; EM-23 cache) is at or above `LIT_ON_PM`; stateless, no hysteresis; unregistered ref: false. *The MVP has no consumer: Sanity's per-visit rule (SN-16, design review) dropped it. The definition is kept here so that a VS-A consumer inherits it; the MVP build neither defines nor calls it, and AC-30's lint adds `lit_static(` to its banned call forms.* | as above |
| `shapes()` | the shape table (EM-8) | static |
| `registered(ref)` | bool — debug builds only | exact |
| ~~`block_hash()`~~ **not exposed by the owner** (ADR-0005 section 1: `canonical_bytes()` and `block_hash()` on an owner become kernel-side reads; an owner that wants to expose "its hash" forwards to the kernel read and computes nothing, and this block exposes neither) *(Amended 2026-10-29 — ADR-0005 sync)* | the kernel's `block_hash(&"emitter.state", uncached = true)`, i.e. `H64(canonical_encode(snapshot payload))` (ADR-0005 section 4.3) | exact |

**EM-26 — Dirty keys, the Lighting contract and the budget agreement.** Dirty keys are emitted for **emitters**, never for individual subjects (publish rule): a key `E/<emitter id>` — an int `(KIND << 32) | id` as in Graph LS-20 — fires on create, remove, `switch_on` flip, `shape_id` change, an `output_pm` change that crosses a bucket (`OUTPUT_DIRTY_QUANTUM_PM`, placeholder 50) and an integer `reach_px` step; continuous pose (origin, aim) never dirties — Lighting polls the read view at render rate, and keys wake only discrete presentation (a light switching on or off, a record spawning). Subject `lux` and `lit` are poll reads: sim consumers read inside their hook, presentation prompts poll at render rate, so a sweeping beam over 192 subjects cannot collapse notifications to `ALL` against `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` 256 (worst case here is every emitter, at most `MAX_EMITTERS` 96, in one tick). **The Lighting contract** (2D Lighting & Occlusion reads and never writes): per emitter `{id, kind, subkind, shape_id, origin_px, aim_units, half_angle_units, reach_px, r_lit_px, r_off_px, curve_class, output_pm, hue_class, lit, section_id, body_id, priority}` plus the shape table (`r_lit_px` and `r_off_px` are the sixteenth and seventeenth fields, the former added by the 2026-10-27 design review and the latter by the 2026-10-28 cross-GDD fix; 2D Lighting's "15-field" wording is refreshed, Cross-References). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* **The foot spill is published by a separate accessor** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: the 17-field record describes a stored emitter and cannot represent the spill (a sub-contribution of the BEAM record centred on the foot, EM-6). `beam_spill(beam_id)` returns, while the beam is on and `BEAM_SPILL_RADIUS_PX` > 0, the derived record `{beam_id, kind BEAM, shape_id 11, origin_px (the foot origin `occ_origin`), reach_px (`BEAM_SPILL_RADIUS_PX`), r_lit_px (the D.7 chain), r_off_px (the same chain at `LIT_OFF_PM`), curve_class SOFT, output_pm (`BEAM_SPILL_PM`), hue_class (the beam's), section_id, body_id, priority (the owning beam's, BEAM default 255)}` and null otherwise; it is not a record, has no id of its own and is **not in `emitters()`** (so `section_emission`, Attention's list and the 96-record cap never see it), and its changes dirty the beam's own key `E/<beam id>`. Its `kind` is the owning beam's BEAM and its `priority` is the beam's (255 by default), so it is never cut before occlusion and never demoted (Ask E-L accepted 2026-10-28); it is read by Lighting only through `beam_spill(beam_id)`, it is a row of `shapes()` (row 11, conditional) but not of `emitters()`. Lighting draws the pool from its `origin_px` and `r_off_px` (edge) and `r_lit_px` (approach prompt), and the build lint of AC-56 checks the drawn edge against max(`r_off_px`, `POOL_RESIDUAL_PX`) ± 1 px (`POOL_RESIDUAL_PX` is Lighting's, 8 px) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*, which is what lets "what you see lit is what the sim calls lit" be tested for the spill (AC-46c). This block publishes facts; Lighting conforms to them. Lighting owns textures, ambient, the canvas modulate, shadow-slot assignment (the sixth slot), the flash clamp (`flash_count` ≤ 3 per rolling second per light), flicker, gutter and decoy visuals; flicker is invisible to the query, which uses the steady mean. **Budget agreement (R17):** the sim never culls by view (an off-screen emitter still exposes — correct for P3); instead authoring lint keeps in-view emitter counts under Lighting's hypotheses (shadow-casting ≤ 6, non-shadow ≤ 24, node lanterns ≤ 8; art bible 8.10 budget shape and 8.11 flags 2 and 8), a debug assertion reports overflow, and every record carries a deterministic `priority` (default by kind: BEAM 255, BEACON 200, FIXTURE 120, DEPLOYABLE 100, FAULT_GLOW 80, NODE_LANTERN 60 — placeholder, owner technical-artist, confirmed by the Lighting spike) so Lighting's "emitters are cut before occlusion" is reproducible; a sim-lit but unrendered light would be a P1 lie, and the residual risk stays in Open Questions. A build lint asserts the rendered reach of every hard-edged row equals the table reach ±1 px.

**EM-27 — The light stimulus for Attention.** The primary read is the per-emitter list (`emitters()`: id, kind, `section_id`, `body_id`, origin, `output_pm`, `reach_px`, shape); the convenience read is `section_emission(section_id)` (Formulas D.12). Attention owns units and weights. The stimulus is **shape-blind by design** (D.12: a narrow beam reads about 2.3 times louder than the fan; default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20), D25) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. **No double counting:** the Graph's `power_use(section_id).lamps_lit_w` is the *power* stimulus; this block's `output_pm`-weighted reach is the *light* stimulus; Attention must not count one lamp as both. The owner's own beam counts once, at its apex value, in the owner's `lux_pm` (EM-21); Attention reads it as emission and does not add it again. Off-screen and unoccupied emitters count. The seat's beam is attributed to the section its foot origin stands in (EM-4, Body's `actor_section`), and the attribution changes in the tick the foot crosses a door, so Attention's per-section ledger and Horror's targeting see the player's exposure where the player is. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* Attention may weight a pool by area rather than radius (the list carries `reach_px` and the shape). (Attention is designed: AT-4 reads `emitters()` and no `probe()`, AT-18 concurs on the beacon.) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*

**EM-28 — Persistence, restore and the binding table.** *Canonical* (snapshotted, hashed): the id counter; per record, the canonical fields of EM-4 (including the FAULT_GLOW records, which are the descriptors they stand for, with their `placed_tick`, the age that protects them from eviction; `arm_tick`; a beam's `last_toggle_tick` (the only source of the `TOO_SOON` strobe guard, EM-7); and a deployable's `evict_tick` and `reach_at_evict`, so an evict-wane in progress survives a save); and the subject registrations (EM-21 table, canonical columns, including each subject's `lit` hysteresis bit, EM-22); no record and no subject stores `body_id` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. *Derived, rebuilt in `post_restore`, never hashed:* beam origin and aim, `origin_px` / `aim_units` / `reach_px` / `output_pm` / record `lit`, every record's and every subject's `body_id` (Layout `body_of`; Body `body_of_actor` for the beam and ACTOR subjects), a beam's and an ACTOR subject's `section_id`, the per-section `static_version` cache of EM-23 W0 *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*, the static-layer pair rows and each subject's unsaturated raw sum, the per-tick read-view snapshot and the per-section emission array (EM-25), and the subject `lux_pm` / `act_lux_pm` / `top_emitter_id` table (the subject's `lit` bit is not rebuilt: it is kept). A snapshot taken before a weld and restored into a Layout that is already welded (Layout restores first, `restore_after`) yields body ids from Layout, never from the snapshot *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. Rejected: `persist false` (`switch_on`, `life_remaining_ticks`, `arm_tick` and the beacon's data have no other source, so save-equivalence would break). `post_restore` runs after all blocks restore (CR-8) and rebuilds the derived set in ascending id, including the whole static layer (the cold class of D.14, scenario S6, so that no subject is pending when the first `validate` runs); the block does not run its hook while RESTORING. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The kernel does not state that `post_restore` calls follow `restore_after`, while Layout re-derives door leaves in its own `post_restore` (Layout LY-26 c): the Emitter's cold build is only correct for open doors if Layout's runs first, so the ordering is requested of the kernel (Open Question 26) and, until it is granted, the restore-time version bump of the narrowing rule (EM-23) re-tests the leaf pairs on tick 1. After a restore the kernel's binding table is rebuilt: the kernel's LOADING rebuild re-binds the seat beams from `beam_bindings()` before the first RUNNING tick (KRN-BIND-01), so there is no window in which `toggle_beam` meets an empty table *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. Save-equivalence (kernel G4) holds with no accepted exception: the `lit` bit is canonical (EM-22), and the hook is ordered after the Graph's last hook on a Graph tick (EM-1). It also depends on one **requirement on the Graph**, now met: its `post_restore` rebuilds `served_pm` and the descriptor list from restored canonical state (Graph LS-21 and its restore edge case, 2026-10-27; Cross-References), without which lamps would read dark and fault glows would be absent for up to `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS - 1` ticks after a load. AC-41 fails if a regression removes the rebuild. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* `schema_version` 1; the restore migration policy is the owner's (kernel CR-8: an unsupported version is a reported failure, never a silent default). The block has a round-trip test (kernel CR-8) and a `state_hash` that covers the canonical set only.

**EM-29 — Isolation: the truth channel.** `emitter.state` is a `SIM` block. The module **never obtains a `PERCEPTION_OUT` view** (kernel CR-12; a lint mirroring PC's acceptance criterion on the Adapter's requested views), never references `Light2D`, `LightOccluder2D`, `Node` or `PhysicsServer2D` (the H10 lint over `src/sim/emitter/`), and runs under a headless test with zero scene nodes. The beam, the real reveal radius and lamp / fixture brightness are on the closed **consequence channel** (the Graph's closed consequence-channel list names "lamp brightness"; the Controller's Perception Filter row: the Filter "may never move the chest point ... or touch the beam"). **A Perception Filter decoy light is a Lighting visual**: it is not an emitter, is absent from `emitter.state`, and exposes nothing; rejected: decoys as `phantom = true` emitters (a perception fact written into a `SIM` block breaks CR-12 and H5). No sentence in this GDD says the Filter may dim, move or add a lamp. The honest cross-check — walk to the real edge and it is where it always was — depends on this. Isolation is by construction, not by policy: no field named `phantom`, `perceived` or `decoy` exists, and the query never takes a Filter-wrapped value (the Graph's `true_value` is the only wrapped path and Emitter State never calls it).

**EM-30 — Frames, zoom, mirror and the determinism contract.** All geometry is integer base px; stored anchors are **section-local** (Layout's frame, LY-3 c) and are composed with `section_offset(section_id)` once per derive, and every comparison runs in the **body frame** (ship-local); an emitter and a subject are compared only if their `body_id` matches. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The `body_id` of every emitter and subject is derived from Layout (EM-4), so all sections welded into one body share one `body_id`: light crosses a weld, the beam lights the objects of a welded derelict and its lamps count toward the player, exactly as Lighting draws it; sections that are not welded (an unwelded derelict, a docked pod) are other bodies and stay dark to each other. A subject on another body (an unwelded or cut-off section, a pod) is not lit by the home frame's emitters (cross-body light between unwelded bodies is VS-A, Open Question 9) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. Zoom, camera, render scale and the integer ladder change **nothing** in the sim; an off-screen lit object stays lit and exposes, and no prompt is drawn off-screen (the HUD's rule). Light positions are integer base px at 60 Hz (`TICK_RATE`); every duration is in ticks via `ticks_for_seconds`. The determinism contract mirrors the Graph's LS-1: integer-only SIM state; **zero floats** stored, hashed, replicated or used on the query path (a designer float in a data file is converted once by `int(round(x * scale))` in the build-time data tool outside `src/sim/emitter/`, which emits the immutable integer tables — `DIR`, the EM-8 `COS2_Q28` column and the like — that the boot step loads and asserts; they are not block state, and no float or trig call exists in the sim module, AC-2); the Q14 direction table, the Q28 cone test, an exact integer floor square root and integer segment-versus-rectangle tests; no global RNG (the block draws none); iteration in ascending id; budgets in counted units; `state_hash` over the canonical set only. Physics-derived observations never enter this block, so the kernel's G3 recording obligation does not apply.

**MVP slice.** MVP (single-player): one seat beam; the home-ship's fixtures (count per room fixed by Derelict Authoring DA-22, registry `mvp_fixture_counts`: home 8, AC-58), derelict A (4 compartments) and B (5) fixtures and node lanterns; the self-powered cryo-bay emergency lamp and one self-powered DOCK_STATUS glow per dock room (X2); the beam's 24 px foot spill (D24); one alarm beacon; glowsticks (`MAX_DEPLOYABLES_LIVE` 8); FAULT_GLOW for the MVP faults with a glow row (`1/FUEL`, `1/GAS`, `2`, `3`, `7`, `9`). VS-A: flares, torches, decoys (`POOL_DEPLOYABLE`), more fixtures, cross-body light. VS-B: four beams, `SHARED_SUMMARY` replication, the corpse-lantern question. Nothing else in this GDD is gated.

### D.5 Cone membership

The `cone_membership` formula is defined as:

`in_cone = (d2 = 0) ∨ ( d2 ≤ R² ∧ D > 0 ∧ D² ≥ d2 × COS2_Q28 )` with `r = anchor − origin`, `d2 = rx² + ry²`, `D = rx × ux + ry × uy`; a 360° shape is `d2 ≤ R²`; BEAM_SPLIT is the OR of two such tests, of which at most one is true (the dark wedge never closes)

**Variables:**

| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `r` | int2 | each component within ±400 | calculated | subject anchor minus emitter origin (EM-8: the single `anchor_px`) |
| `d2` | int | 0..147,456 | calculated | squared distance; 0 is inside every cone (the apex) |
| `R` | int px | 24..384 (I-REACH) | `reach_px` | the hard reach; the edge is closed (`d2 = R²` is inside) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the first draft's 96 floor ignored the 24 px waning floor and the 72 px fault glow)* |
| `(ux, uy)` | Q14 int pair | ±16384 | D.4 | the axis |
| `D` | int | within ±6,291,456 | calculated | Q14 dot product; the `D > 0` guard is required (the squared test alone accepts the opposite half-plane) |
| `COS2_Q28` | int | per shape row | EM-8 table (square of the Q14 cosine of `half_angle_units`) | 201,441,249 wide; 256,768,576 narrow; 260,305,956 split; 66,994,225 fan; 236,913,664 beacon |

**Output Range:** bool. Every product is below 2^62 (`D²` and `d2 × COS2_Q28` ≤ 3.96 × 10^13; I-OVERFLOW). The quantised edge misplaces a rim by under 0.1° (under 0.7 px at 384 px). **Example (wide cone, origin (300, 166), aim 0):** subject (540, 200) → `r` (240, 34), `d2` 58,756 ≤ 82,944, `D²` 15,461,882,265,600 ≥ 58,756 × 201,441,249 = 11,835,882,026,244 → inside; subject (540, 28) → `r` (240, −138), `d2` 76,644, product 15,439,263,088,356 ≤ `D²` → inside (29.90°); subject (540, 27) → `r` (240, −139), product 15,495,062,314,329 > `D²` → outside (30.08°; the encoded edge is 29.97°). One pixel flips the answer, which is the sim/render agreement test.

### D.6 Occluder segment test

The `occluder_segment_test` formula is defined as:

`blocked = ∃ K′ ∈ boxes(OccluderSource.rects_in(aabb(S, P))) : t_lo ≤ t_hi`, evaluated on **doubled coordinates** `S′ = 2S`, `P′ = 2P` against the unit-square box of each rectangle, `K′ = [2·x0 − 1, 2·x1 − 1] × [2·y0 − 1, 2·y1 − 1]` for a stored `[x0, x1) × [y0, y1)` (EM-20 a); `t_lo = max(0, tx_lo, ty_lo)`, `t_hi = min(1, tx_hi, ty_hi)`; per axis `a` with `d_a = P′_a − S′_a`: if `d_a = 0` the interval is all of ℝ when `min_a ≤ S′_a ≤ max_a` and empty otherwise, else `t = (min_a − S′_a) / d_a` and `(max_a − S′_a) / d_a` ordered by the sign of `d_a`; fractions are compared by cross-multiplication with positive denominators (no division) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*

**Variables:**

| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `S` | int2, px | ship-local | D.4 `occ_origin` (the foot for the beam, the anchor for other kinds) | segment start |
| `P` | int2, px | ship-local | subject `anchor_px` | segment end; at least `ANCHOR_CLEARANCE_PX` outside every rectangle (authoring lint) |
| `K′` | int4, doubled px | the closed unit-square box `[2·x0 − 1, 2·x1 − 1] × [2·y0 − 1, 2·y1 − 1]` of a stored half-open rectangle `[x0,x1) × [y0,y1)` — equivalently the occupied span `(x0, y0, x1−1, y1−1)` that Layout returns (registry `rect_algebra_closed_span`) widened by one doubled unit, half a pixel, on every side; `min_a`, `max_a` are its bounds *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | Layout via `OccluderSource` | wall (`WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH` 24), closed door leaf, `occludes_light` prop; actors and horrors never occlude |

**Output Range:** bool. Closed unit-square boxes and a conservative rule: a touch (corner graze, edge-on pass) is blocked (EM-20 a); an endpoint in an occupied cell is inside a box and is blocked; an endpoint outside every box is never on a box face (even doubled coordinates against odd box bounds). All cross-products are below 2^42 (doubled offsets within ±2^11), inside I-OVERFLOW. **Example (axis-aligned; the first draft's probes, re-derived):** wall stored [408,432) × [96,288) (occupied span x 408..431, y 96..287; doubled box x [815, 863], y [191, 575]); `S` (302, 200), `S′` (604, 400). `P` (540, 200), `P′` (1080, 400): `d_x` 476, x-slab [211/476, 259/476] = [0.443, 0.544], `d_y` 0 with 191 ≤ 400 ≤ 575 → `t_lo` 0.443 ≤ `t_hi` 0.544 → blocked. `P` (407, 200), `P′` 814: x-slab [211/210, 259/210] = [1.005, 1.233], `t_lo` 1.005 > `t_hi` 1 → not blocked. `P` (408, 200), `P′` 816: x-slab [211/212, 259/212], `t_lo` 0.995 ≤ `t_hi` 1 → blocked (the anchor is in the wall's own cell, which the clearance lint refuses). From the east, `S` (500, 200) to `P` (432, 200) (`S′` 1000, `P′` 864, `d_x` −136): x-slab [1.007, 1.360], `t_lo` > `t_hi` 1 → not blocked (anchor 432 has clearance 1). **Example (oblique, the leak the first draft hid):** a horizontal wall run stored as two rectangles [0,24) × [240,264) and [24,48) × [240,264) (doubled boxes x [−1, 47] and [47, 95], y [479, 527]); `S` (23, 300), `P` (24, 140). On the first draft's closed spans (x 0..23 and 24..47) the ray crossed the wall rows at x 23.23..23.38, inside the strip between the spans, and touched neither: a leak. On the boxes: `S′` (46, 600), `P′` (48, 280), `d_x` 2, `d_y` −320; box 1 has x-slab [(−1−46)/2, (47−46)/2] = [−23.5, 0.5] and y-slab [(527−600)/−320, (479−600)/−320] = [0.228, 0.378] → `t_lo` 0.228 ≤ `t_hi` 0.378 → blocked. **Example (diagonal corner join):** A [0,24) × [0,24) and B [24,48) × [24,48) meet only at a corner (doubled boxes [−1, 47]² and [47, 95]², sharing the point (47, 47)); `S` (24, 23) to `P` (23, 24), `S′` (48, 46), `P′` (46, 48), passes exactly through that point: box A has x-slab [0.5, 24.5] and y-slab [−2

### D.7 Illumination

The `illumination` formula is defined as:

`c = ⌊ output_pm × f / 1000 ⌋`, SOFT: `f = F(d, R)`; HARD: `f = EDGE_FLOOR_PM + ⌊(1000 − EDGE_FLOOR_PM) × F(d, R) / 1000⌋`; `F(d, R) = ⌊1000 × (R − d) / R⌋` (curve id LINEAR, the MVP default); `d = max{k : SQ[k] ≤ d2}`; `lux_pm = min(1000, Σ c)`; `act_lux_pm = min(1000, Σ c over gates_actions emitters)`; actionable radius `r_lit = max{ d ∈ 0..R : c(d) ≥ LIT_ON_PM }` over the same integer chain (−1 when `c(0) < LIT_ON_PM`), found by binary search because `c` is monotone non-increasing in `d`, and **published from the sim per emitter as `r_lit_px`** (derived on an output or reach change; the closed form ⌊R × (output_pm − LIT_ON_PM) / output_pm⌋ is retired) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; latch-release radius `r_off = max{ d ∈ 0..R : c(d) ≥ LIT_OFF_PM }` over the same integer chain (−1 when `c(0) < LIT_OFF_PM`), found by a second binary search bounded to the window [max(0, `r_lit_px`), min(`R`, max(0, `r_lit_px`) + ⌊`R` × (`LIT_ON_PM` − `LIT_OFF_PM`) / `output_pm`⌋ + 2)] because `c` is monotone, and **published per emitter as `r_off_px`** (`r_off_px ≥ r_lit_px` always) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*

**Variables:**

| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `output_pm` | int | 0..1000 | D.1, D.3, D.9 (constant), D.11, `BEAM_BASE_PM` | the emitter's steady output |
| `d` | int px | 0..R | `SQ` table: 385 squares, binary search, 9 probes | exact integer floor of the distance from the origin (the chest for the beam); no square root, no float |
| `R` | int px | 24..384 | `reach_px` | current reach (D.9 for a waning stick) |
| `F` | int | 0..1000 | curve id (data) | 1000 at the apex, 0 at `R`; a replacement curve (a 17-knot table, linear interpolation on `u = ⌊d × 1024 / R⌋`) keeps the signature and must stay monotone, integer, with non-negative operands (R15) |
| `EDGE_FLOOR_PM` | int | 250 (160..400) | placeholder, owner technical-artist, confirmed by the Lighting spike | the HARD-class contribution kept at the rim; jointly bound with `LIT_ON_PM` by I-EDGE |
| `LIT_ON_PM` | int | 150 (100..300) | D.8 | the turn-on threshold |
| `r_lit_px` | int px | −1..R | calculated, published per emitter | the largest `d` whose integer chain gives `c ≥ LIT_ON_PM`; the approach radius: where a prompt for a not-yet-lit subject first appears (no longer what Lighting draws a soft pool's boundary at: that is `r_off_px`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* |
| `r_off_px` | int px | −1..R | calculated, published per emitter | the largest `d` whose integer chain gives `c ≥ LIT_OFF_PM`; where a soft pool is drawn (Lighting draws at max(`r_off_px`, `POOL_RESIDUAL_PX`)) and how far a prompt for an already-lit subject persists (the D.8 latch); it follows the same HARD / SOFT convention as `r_lit_px`; derived like `r_lit_px` (recomputed on an output or reach change and in `post_restore`, not snapshotted, not canonical state) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* |

**Output Range:** `c` 0..1000, `lux_pm` and `act_lux_pm` 0..1000 (saturating; addition commutes, so there is no order dependence). There is no ambient term (`AMBIENT_PM` 0). The owner's own beam adds its full `output_pm` (the d = 0 apex value) to the owner's ACTOR `lux_pm` and nothing to its `act_lux_pm` (EM-21). **Example:** wide beam `output_pm` 1000, `d2` 43,264 → `d` 208 (208² ≤ 43,264 < 209²), `R` 288: `F` ⌊1000 × 80 / 288⌋ = 277, `f` 250 + ⌊750 × 277 / 1000⌋ = 457, `c` 457; at the rim `c` = `EDGE_FLOOR_PM` 250 (lit), and a beam at `output_pm` 600 has rim `c` 150 (lit) while 599 gives 149 (unlit), the ⌈`LIT_ON_PM` × 1000 / `EDGE_FLOOR_PM`⌉ = 600 consequence. SOFT fixture `R` 144, `output_pm` 1000: `d` 122 → `F` 152 (lit), `d` 123 → 145 (unlit), `r_lit` 122 (the chain: `d` 122 lit, `d` 123 unlit; at output 1000 the closed form ⌊144 × 850 / 1000⌋ = 122 agrees with the chain for every `R` from 24 to 384, but at output 450 the closed form gives 96 where the chain gives 95; over `R` = 24..384 step 24 and `output_pm` 151..1000 the closed form ran 1 px high in 1,405 of 13,600 cases and never low, the review's coarser sweep found 219 of 5,100, so Lighting's drawn pool edge would have sat 1 px outside the actionable edge and used the whole AC-56 tolerance) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. **Latch-release radius `r_off_px`** (fixture R 144, from `c(d)` = ⌊output × ⌊1000 × (144 − d) / 144⌋ / 1000⌋ ≥ 120): outputs 1000 / 600 / 300 / 200 / 160 / 150 / 140 / 121 / 120 give `r_off_px` 126 / 115 / 86 / 57 / 36 / 28 / 20 / 1 / 0, against `r_lit_px` 122 / 108 / 72 / 36 / 8 / 0 / −1 / −1 / −1 (at output 1000, `c`(126) = ⌊1000 × 125 / 1000⌋ = 125 ≥ 120 and `c`(127) = ⌊1000 × 118 / 1000⌋ = 118 < 120); output 450 gives 95 and 105; a glowstick R 96 at 1000 gives `r_lit_px` 81 and `r_off_px` 84; the foot spill R 24 at 600 gives 18 and 19. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* Sum: beam 457 + a lamp of `output_pm` 848 at `d` 100 (`F` 305, `c` ⌊848 × 305 / 1000⌋ = 258) → `lux_pm` 715; adding a fixture at `d` 60 (`c` 583) gives 1298 → 1000. Alone with the lamp on, the owner reads `lux_pm` 1000.

### D.8 Lit with hysteresis

The `lit_hysteresis` formula is defined as:

`lit′ = (act_lux_pm ≥ LIT_ON_PM) ∨ (lit ∧ act_lux_pm ≥ LIT_OFF_PM)`; a stateless `lit_on = act_lux_pm ≥ LIT_ON_PM` form is reserved for the VS-A `probe(body_id, point)` (EM-24) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*

**Variables:**

| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `act_lux_pm` | int | 0..1000 | D.7 | action-gating light (the BEACON does not gate) |
| `lit` | bool | 0/1 | canonical, one bit per subject (EM-22) | last tick's answer; kept across a restore |
| `LIT_ON_PM` | int | 150 (100..300) | placeholder, owner technical-artist (art bible 7.0), confirmed by the Lighting spike | turn-on |
| `LIT_OFF_PM` | int | 120 (60..140), `< LIT_ON_PM` | same | turn-off; there is no dwell (`LIT_OFF_DWELL_TICKS` fixed at 0) |

**Output Range:** bool. The band in px at a soft rim is `r_off_px` − `r_lit_px` (the same integer chains at `LIT_OFF_PM` and `LIT_ON_PM`; never the closed form ⌊`R` × (`LIT_ON_PM` − `LIT_OFF_PM`) / `output_pm`⌋, which runs 1 px low for some outputs), bounded by ⌊`R` × (`LIT_ON_PM` − `LIT_OFF_PM`) / `output_pm`⌋ + 2: 4 px for a fixture (R 144: 126 − 122) and 3 px for a glowstick (R 96: 84 − 81) at output 1000 *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; a hard rim is a step (457 → 0 across one pixel), so hysteresis only matters for dimmed or soft light. **Example:** 160 → lit; 130 → still lit; 119 → unlit; 140 → still unlit; 151 → lit. A subject saved lit at 130 is lit after the restore (the bit is canonical). A lamp browning from `served_pm` 950 to 780 moves a subject at `d` 122 from `c` 144 (still lit) to 118 (unlit).

### D.15 Boot invariants

The `boot_invariants` formula is defined as:

`I-EDGE ∧ I-HYST ∧ I-WEDGE ∧ I-OVERFLOW ∧ I-MIRROR ∧ I-CAPS ∧ I-WANE ∧ I-REACH ∧ I-DOCK ∧ I-SPACING` *(I-DOCK and I-SPACING added 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* — every one is checked at data load; a violated invariant refuses the build or the boot (no run-time fallback), **except I-SPACING, which is a build warning** (it depends on a value the Player Controller owns and is promoted to a refusal when that value is raised), and each has an acceptance criterion *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the first draft said every violated invariant refuses; AC-52 now carries a Result column of REFUSE, WARN, FALLBACK and PASS)*. **Implemented as explicit fault checks, never as `assert()`** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: GDScript `assert()` is stripped from Release export templates, so an invariant written as an assert disappears in the shipped build and a test on a Debug build cannot see it. Each invariant is a function in the boot-check file that returns a fault code; the composition root refuses to start (and the build lint fails) on any non-OK code in Debug and Release alike; a lint bans `assert(` in the boot-check file; the checks take an injected Diagnostics seam carrying a `build_is_debug` flag, so a test runs the same code with the flag false (as in a Release build); and one Release-template smoke criterion (AC-52f) proves the checks run in the real export
