## Decision

The Emitter is one `SIM` block, one hook, a published mutator object, three commands and a pure exposure kernel. Sixteen numbered decision sections follow (`D<section>.<n>`); the requirement tables cite them.

### Architecture Diagram

```
 composition root (BOOTING)                    stage-1 content (ADR-0007 section 1.7, frozen before the kernel)
   EmitterModule.setup(facet, catalogs, ports) <-- ShapeCatalog, HueMap, EmitterTuning, GlowTable (F&T rows)
        | register_block / register_command x3 / register_hook / register_key_space / register_fault_domain(6)
        v
 +--------------------------- src/sim/emitter/ ----------------------------------------------------------+
 |  EmitterState (PERSISTED, 1 block)       EmitterDerived (never saved, never hashed)   EmitterScratch  |
 |   hdr: next_emitter_id, last_place_tick,  slot stores (emitters, subjects),            per-tick sums,  |
 |        fault_step_seen                    point grids (per section, local px),        candidate lists,|
 |   emitters: 25 columns, ascending id      pair rows (subject-major, stride K),        one QueryBuffer |
 |   subjects: 11 columns, ascending ref     raw sums, record derived fields,            EmitterDiag     |
 |                                           section cache (version triple, offset)      (never hashed)  |
 |                                                                                                       |
 |  hook emitter.place  W0 read, frames > W1 lifecycle > W2 derive > W3 find changes > W4 deltas          |
 |  (divisor 1, offset 0)  > W5 dynamic layer > W6 sums, hysteresis, commit > W7 dirty keys, emission    |
 |  mutators E1..E10 (scope.open_for first)      commands toggle_beam, set_switch, set_beacon            |
 +--------------^-----------------------------------------------------------------^---------------------+
      reads     | LayoutView, OccluderSource, GraphView, BodyView, ControllerView,  | pure calls
                | SuitView, ClockView                                               |
 +--------------+------------------ src/shared/emitter/ (L0, static funcs, no state) +--------------------+
 | DirTable (generated)  ConeMath  SegmentMath  Illumination  LampMath  WaneMath  BeaconMath  ExposureProbe|
 +----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
 readers: Interaction (validate, hook), Horror, Attention, Suit, Sanity, Web Map, Lighting (render rate)
          through EmitterView (getter-only, typed scalars and caller-owned buffers, CNT-03)
```

### 1. Module layout, purity split and what is data (TR-emitter-003, -006, -016, -017, -030, -034, TR-itemdb-034, TR-derelict-038)

| Location | Contents | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `src/shared/emitter/` (L0) | `emitter_kind.gd` (closed enums and transition tables), `dir_table.gd` (**generated**, `const UX: Array[int]`, `const UY: Array[int]`), `cone_math.gd`, `segment_math.gd`, `illumination.gd`, `lamp_math.gd`, `wane_math.gd`, `beacon_math.gd`, `exposure_probe.gd` | static functions over ints only; no state, no I/O, no `Node`; imports nothing but `IntMath`. This is the "published table and kernel" that `src/data` and the content lint may name (ADR-0007 section 1.9: `src/data` never imports `src/sim`). |
| `src/data/emitter/` | `shape_table_schema.gd`, `hue_map_schema.gd`, `emitter_tuning_schema.gd`, `glow_table_schema.gd`; catalogs `ShapeCatalog`, `HueMap`, `EmitterTuning`, `GlowTable` | stage-1 closed schemas and frozen catalogs (ADR-0007 sections 1.4, 1.5); array exposure per CNT-03 (`Array[int]` read-only, or index accessors) |
| `src/sim/emitter/` | `emitter_module.gd` (setup, registrations, hook, command callables), `emitter_state.gd`, `emitter_derived.gd`, `emitter_scratch.gd`, `emitter_diag.gd`, `emitter_mutators.gd`, `emitter_faults.gd`, `emitter_reasons.gd`, `emitter_units.gd`, `emitter_outcome.gd`, `emitter_verify.gd`, `emitter_boot_checks.gd`, `views/emitter_view.gd`, `views/emitter_view_empty.gd`, `testing/test_brute_exposure.gd`, `testing/test_*.gd` doubles | scene-tree free; passes the whole SIM lint pack (SIM-01..15) with no waiver |
| `tools/emitter/` | `gen_dir_table.gd`, `check_shapes.gd` | the **only** place a float or trig call exists for this system; outside `src/`, so SIM-03 does not apply; CI regenerates and diffs |

**D1.1 Purity split.** The exposure kernel is pure functions of ints so that unit tests, the content lint (TR-derelict-038: "console, arrival and wake-room lighting proved headlessly") and the block call the same code. `ExposureProbe` composes the kernel with a caller-supplied `OccluderSource` double and plain emitter fields; it is **not** the VS-A `probe(body_id, point)` read (deferred and lint-banned in MVP source) and is importable from `src/sim/` only inside `testing/` and the boot checks.

**D1.2 What is data (decided).** The shape table (11 rows, EM-8), the hue token set and every tunable are **stage-1 content**, not code constants: `assets/data/emitter/{shape_table,hue_map,emitter_tuning}.json` plus the Failure & Trail glow rows in `assets/data/failure_trail/glow_table.json` (ADR-0007 section 1.1; architecture IC-12). Reasons: gameplay values are data-driven (coding standards); the technical artist owns the placeholders and re-tunes after the Lighting spike; and the Item DB `emits` clause (TR-emitter-043, TR-itemdb-034) needs a table to validate against at load, which ADR-0007 section 1.4 says the loader must **read from the Emitter's published table and not copy** (stage 1 loads before the Item DB, section 1.7). **`ShapeCatalog` is that published table.** Its authored columns are `shape_id`, `curve_class`, `geometry` (`ONE_CONE`, `TWO_CONES`, `OMNI`), `half_angle_units`, `split_axis_units`, `reach_px`, `gates_actions`, `shadow_casting` (informational) and `art_ref`; the freeze **derives** `cos2_q28` from `DirTable` (the square of the Q14 cosine at `half_angle_units`) instead of storing a second hand-typed integer, so the table, the direction table and the I-OVERFLOW bound cannot disagree. The five derived values equal the GDD's EM-8 column exactly (probed, section 11). The art-bible degrees stay in the art bible; `tools/emitter/check_shapes.gd` checks each `half_angle_units` against its degree figure (float allowed there) and fails the build on drift over its tolerance.

**D1.3 The direction table is generated code, not content (decided).** `DirTable.UX`/`UY` are mathematical constants (two `AIM_UNITS`-entry `Array[int]` consts), not designer data, so they bypass the content loader: a lint or test can use them with no `ContentSet`, and an engine change cannot reorder a JSON array under them. ADR-0007 Alternative 2 (code-as-data) is rejected for *content*; it does not cover a derived mathematical table, and `tools/emitter/gen_dir_table.gd` plus a CI byte-diff gate (`EMT-GOLD-01`) make regeneration a build step with a golden hash. Generation: the first quadrant `a = 0..AIM_UNITS/4` is computed in the tool as `round(16384 * cos/sin(a * TAU / AIM_UNITS))`, and the other three are filled **by reflection**, never recomputed (`DIR[AIM_UNITS/2 - a] = (-ux, uy)`, `DIR[AIM_UNITS - a] = (ux, -uy)`), then `uy` is negated so that aim `3 * AIM_UNITS / 4` is `(0, +16384)` (south, screen y down, EM-19). I-MIRROR is therefore true by construction and re-asserted at boot. **Probed:** `const X: PackedInt32Array = PackedInt32Array([...])` fails to parse ("isn't a constant expression"); `const X: Array[int] = [...]` loads (4,096 elements, `is_read_only()` true). The kernel reads `DirTable.UX[a]` directly in `@hot` code (an indexed read of a typed constant array: no copy, no allocation). The table length must equal `AIM_UNITS` (boot invariant `I-DIRSIZE`).

**D1.4 Square-root table (decided).** The distance `d = floor(sqrt(d2))` of D.7 is the largest `k` with `k*k <= d2`, found by the native `bsearch` of a boot-built `PackedInt32Array` of squares (`SQ[k] = k*k`, `k = 0..REACH_MAX_PX + 1`) owned by `EmitterDerived` and passed to the kernel (`static var` is banned, so the table is an instance field, not a global). Exactness is a boot invariant (`I-SQRT`: for every `d2` in `0..REACH_MAX_PX^2` the result `r` satisfies `r*r <= d2 < (r+1)*(r+1)`). Probed 2026-10-29: 0 failures over all 147,457 values, **63 ns** per call against **397 ns** for a binary-search loop and 144 ns for `bsearch` on the read-only `Array[int]` (so the packed table is built once at boot, cold, and held by the instance). No `sqrt`, float or `Vector2` appears on the path (SIM-03/04).

### 2. The block: what is canonical and what is derived (TR-emitter-001, -005, -007, -028 (canonical part), -030, -037)

**D2.1 Descriptor values** (the per-block values ADR-0003 leaves to the owner; TR-emitter-001): `block_id &"emitter.state"`, `owner_name &"emitter"`, `schema_version 1`, `supported_versions [1]`, `block_class SIM`, `persist true`, `persist_scope WORLD`, `scope SHARED`, `gameplay true`, `interpolated false` (so `commit_baseline`/`snap_baseline` are not registered), `repl_hint SHARED_SUMMARY`, `restore_after [layout.state, graph.state, body.state, controller.state]`, `added_in_format 1` (the format data file entry of Save/Load SL-15; the boot lints `SL_BOOT_NO_SUPPORTED_VERSIONS` and `SL_BOOT_NO_ADDED_IN_FORMAT` therefore pass), `init_world` **not** registered (Web Map's `init_world` calls E1 and E10 under the shared INIT scope; the seat beam is created by E9 from the new-game step, D3.4), `binding_source` registered (D3.5). `read_view` returns the long-lived `EmitterView` (section 13); `empty_view` its `EmitterViewEmpty` twin.

**D2.2 One class per concern (decided).** `EmitterState` holds the persisted columns only (typed packed arrays and ints; no cache, no scratch, no `Dictionary`); `EmitterDerived` holds every rebuildable structure; `EmitterScratch` holds per-tick temporaries sized once; `EmitterDiag` holds counters (never hashed). This is ADR-0011's four-class pattern applied to a smaller block. It makes "persisted versus derived" checkable by reflection and by a **zero-and-diff** test (zero every `EmitterDerived` column, call `post_restore`, assert the block hash and every read-view answer unchanged), which is the executable form of TR-emitter-007.

**D2.3 The persisted set (closed; the snapshot key set is generated from this table and an allow-list test walks it, as ADR-0013 AC-130).** `snapshot(ctx)` calls `ctx.put` with a String-keyed Dictionary, every packed column a `duplicate()`, rows in ascending id or ref, no `Dictionary` keyed by an id, no `StringName`/`PackedStringArray`/`Vector2i`/`Rect2i`/`Resource` (ADR-0006 section 1.2, ADR-0013 section 2).

| Key | Type | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `schema_version` | `int` | `EMITTER_SCHEMA_VERSION` |
| `hdr` | `Dictionary` of three `int`s | `next_emitter_id` (first id 1; never reused; EM-4), `last_place_tick` (the tick of the last completed `emitter.place`, -1 before the first; D2.5), `fault_step_seen` (the Graph `last_step_no` last reconciled for FAULT_GLOW, -1 before the first; D6.4) |
| `emitters` | `Dictionary` of 25 columns | `PackedInt32Array`: `id`, `owner_ref`, `section_id`, `anchor_x`, `anchor_y`, `base_pm`, `node_ref`, `life_remaining_ticks`, `life_total_ticks`, `reach_at_evict`, `glow_key`, `sev`, `beacon_phase`, `hue_id`; `PackedByteArray`: `kind`, `subkind`, `shape_id`, `switch_on`, `beacon_dir` (0 = -1, 1 = +1), `priority`, `pending`; `PackedInt64Array`: `last_toggle_tick`, `arm_tick`, `evict_tick`, `placed_tick`. Ascending `id`. A column a kind does not use holds the sentinel the GDD names (-1 for `life_*`, `evict_tick`, `last_toggle_tick` until set; 0 elsewhere); the snapshot writer writes the sentinel, never stale data. |
| `subjects` | `Dictionary` of 11 columns | `PackedInt64Array`: `ref` (kind-tagged, opaque to the block; ascending, unique); `PackedByteArray`: `kind`, `moving`, `lit` (the hysteresis bit), `pending` (0 applied, 1 register-pending, 2 unregister-pending), `has_pend_anchor`; `PackedInt32Array`: `section_id`, `anchor_x`, `anchor_y`, `pend_x`, `pend_y`. For an ACTOR row `section_id`, `anchor_x`, `anchor_y` are **derived** (read from Body every tick) and are written as 0. |

Everything else is `EmitterDerived`: `body_id` of every record and subject (never stored, never hashed, EM-4), `origin_px`, `aim_units`, `half_angle_units`, `reach_px`, `output_pm`, record `lit`, `r_lit_px`, `r_off_px`, `curve_class`, top ids, the slot stores, grids, pair rows, raw sums, per-subject `lux_pm`/`act_lux_pm`/`top_emitter_id`, the section cache, the section-emission array, last-emitted dirty buckets, the version cache (D11.4) and every scratch buffer. `state_hash` over this block is the kernel's `block_hash` of `canonical_encode(snapshot payload)` (ADR-0005 section 4.3); **the block exposes no `canonical_bytes()` and no `block_hash()`** (EM-25 as amended 2026-10-29), and the round-trip test uses the kernel-side reads `canonical_encode` and `block_hash(&"emitter.state", uncached = true)` (TR-emitter-038, owned by ADR-0003/0005; this ADR supplies the payload).

**D2.4 Capacity and size.** Row counts are bounded by `MAX_EMITTERS` and `MAX_EXPOSURE_SUBJECTS` (registry); a snapshot at both caps is tens of KB of column data at the very most (about 96 x 100 plus 192 x 40 bytes), far below the payload ceiling (ADR-0002 `payload_size_check`, ADR-0006 `MAX_BLOCK_BYTES`); `snapshot()` computes the byte estimate from the counts and raises the one-shot diagnostic `emitter_block_soft_bytes` over `EMITTER_BLOCK_SOFT_BYTES` (an `EmitterTuning` key).

**D2.5 Pending-intent columns: the finding that changes the canonical list (decided; GDD sync).** EM-28 lists the canonical set without them, and EM-5/EM-23 say the subject table "first reflects spawns, E7 unregisters and E8 anchor moves at the first `emitter.place` at or after that tick". Hooks ordered **after** `emitter.place` call mutators in the same tick (Interaction's landing hook: E3 and E6/E7; Horror's hook: E6/E7/E8). A snapshot taken at the end of that tick holds the late mutation in the record columns while the live subject table does not yet reflect it; a restore that cold-builds the table from every row would reflect it at once, so `validate` at tick T+1 would answer differently in the live and the restored run: **kernel G4 breaks** under the GDD's own wording. This ADR therefore makes the lag canonical and small: `emitters.pending` (1 = created since the last committed `emitter.place`), `subjects.pending`/`has_pend_anchor`/`pend_x`/`pend_y` (a registration, an unregistration or an anchor move not yet applied to the table) and `hdr.last_place_tick`. Rules: a creation mutator sets `pending = 1` and fills the record's **derived** fields synchronously (TR-emitter-037: the read view is complete from P4 of the creating tick) but the record contributes to no pair row, no subject sum and no `section_emission` until W3 of the next run, which clears every `pending`; E6 on a new ref sets `subjects.pending = 1` (counted against the caps and the duplicate check at once, absent from the table: `lux`/`lit` read 0/false); E7 sets `pending = 2` (the row stays in the table until the next run, then is removed); E8 writes `pend_x/pend_y` and `has_pend_anchor = 1` (the applied `anchor_x/y` is what the table was built from). A mutator that runs **before** `emitter.place` in its tick (any P2 apply; a hook the sort places earlier) is applied by that tick's own W3, so no `pending` row survives a tick in which its creator ran earlier. `post_restore` builds the table from the **applied** view (emitters with `pending` 0; subjects with `pending` 0 or 2; the applied anchor) and derives with `T_derive = hdr.last_place_tick`; the next run applies the pending rows exactly as the uninterrupted run would. The cost is one byte per row, a header int and ten bytes per subject; the gain is that G4 holds with no exception list. The permutation harness of ADR-0016 (KRN-RST-05) gets a mandatory fixture: an E6, an E7, an E8 and an E3 issued by a hook ordered after `emitter.place` on the snapshot tick.

**D2.6 Ids and iteration (TR-emitter-005).** `next_emitter_id` is allocated by the block (kernel CR-8), starts at 1, is persisted, is never reused and is checked at restore (`EMITTER_RESTORE_COUNTER`: it exceeds every stored id). Records are appended in ascending id and removed by deleting the row; every iteration is over rows in ascending id or subjects in ascending ref (the persisted order), through the rank indexes of the slot stores (D10.1). No `Dictionary` is iterated anywhere in `src/sim/emitter/` (lint `EMT-02` extends SIM-09 and DET-01 to the directory); `sort_custom`, `shuffle` and `pick_random` are banned by DET-01 already.

**D2.7 Closed kind set and the no-perception-field rule (TR-emitter-006, EM-29).** `EmitterKind` is a closed enum: `BEAM, FIXTURE, NODE_LANTERN, DEPLOYABLE, BEACON, FAULT_GLOW`; subkinds `FIXTURE_EMERGENCY`, `FIXTURE_DOCK_STATUS`, `DEPLOYABLE_GLOWSTICK` (`FLARE`, `TORCH`, `DECOY` are VS-A and absent until a schema bump). Ids are code constants locked by `assets/data/emitter/ids.lock.json` (ADR-0007 section 3 ledger), so an enum reorder cannot silently change a saved byte. The column list above is the whole record; lint `EMT-04` fails any identifier `phantom`, `perceived`, `decoy`, `hallucinated` and any `PERCEPTION_OUT`/`PerceptionRef`/`true_value` token in `src/sim/emitter/` and `src/shared/emitter/`.

### 3. Registration, commands and mutators (TR-emitter-002, -004, -009, -010, -011, -012, -013, -035, -037, TR-interact-036, TR-boarding-013, TR-webmap-028, TR-light-033)

**D3.1 One hook.** `HookDescriptor{hook_id &"emitter.place", divisor 1, offset 0, after [{id &"body.integrate", tolerates_stale false}, {id &"graph.propagate.failure", tolerates_stale true}]}`. `body.integrate` runs every tick (the hooks coincide), so its edge is not stale-tolerant; the failure hook runs once per `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS`, so its edge declares `tolerates_stale` (ADR-0003 guideline). Because the compiled order is global, `emitter.place` is after the power and atmo hooks on every tick on which they run, and after `controller.step` and `layout.doors` through `body.integrate` (ADR-0014 section 7, same-tick truth). In MIRROR mode the hook is not run (ADR-0001) and a replica reads the replicated `SHARED_SUMMARY`; what that summary carries is a VS-B ask recorded in Open Questions, not decided here. No second Emitter hook exists in the MVP.

**D3.2 Commands** (`CommandTypeDescriptor`; validate and apply are `Callable`s ending `return ctx.complete()`; reasons are `StringName` domain codes under `VALIDATION_FAILED(reason)` and live in `EmitterReasons`):

| Command | Origins | `actor_binding` / `actor_source` | `coalesce` | `max_age_ticks` | `writes_blocks` | Validation order (first failure rejects) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `toggle_beam` | `ORIGIN_PLAYER` | `OWNED_BY_ISSUER` / `emitter.state` (the key is `(emitter.state, beam_id)`, kernel CR-7) | `NONE` | 120 | `[emitter.state]` | `NO_SUCH_EMITTER`, `NOT_ACTIONABLE` (`loco_state` in STAGGERED, DOWNED, DEAD; IN_POD is accepted), `TOO_SOON`, `CHARGE_EMPTY` (turn-ON only) |
| `set_switch` | `PLAYER` (payload `{emitter_id}`, a toggle against the true `switch_on`) and `SYSTEM` (payload `{emitter_id, on}`) | `PLAYER`: `OWNED_BY_ISSUER` / `body.state`; `SYSTEM`: none | `NONE` | 120 | `[emitter.state, graph.state]` | `NO_SUCH_EMITTER`, `NOT_SWITCHABLE` (kind not FIXTURE, or any DOCK_STATUS fixture), `COOLDOWN`, `NOT_LIVE` (**`SYSTEM` only**) |
| `set_beacon` | `SYSTEM` | none | `NONE` | 120 | `[emitter.state, graph.state]` | `NO_SUCH_EMITTER`, `NOT_BEACON`, `NOT_LIVE` |

`allowed_when_paused` is false for all three. `graph.state` is listed in `writes_blocks` for the two commands whose apply calls M14, so the strict-debug `WRITES_BLOCKS_UNDECLARED` check (ADR-0003 section 10) passes. Payload schemas are closed (`emitter_id: INT required 1..max`, `on: BOOL required`). The codes `TOO_SOON`, `COOLDOWN`, `NOT_ACTIONABLE`, `NOT_LIVE`, `NOT_SWITCHABLE`, `NOT_BEACON`, `NO_SUCH_EMITTER`, `CHARGE_EMPTY` are this ADR's domain vocabulary (the Controller's tests and Interaction cite them by name). **Every command reaches exactly one terminal result** (ADR-0002); a same-state `SYSTEM` `set_switch`/`set_beacon` is Applied with no state change, **no dirty key and no `last_toggle_tick` write**; a mutator called outside a `WriteScope` is `REFUSED` with no state change in a release build (TR-emitter-035; the exactly-one-result rule is ADR-0002's, the scope rule ADR-0003's, the same-state semantics are this block's).

**D3.3 No oracle (TR-emitter-012).** `validate` for a `PLAYER` `set_switch` evaluates only "structurally present" kind facts (`NO_SUCH_EMITTER`, `NOT_SWITCHABLE`, `COOLDOWN`); it **never reads** `node_state`, `served_pm`, `run_pm` or any health field (Interaction IA-11(a)). The apply flips `switch_on` and calls M14 whatever the node is (a stale or SALVAGED node is a Graph no-op); the lamp stays dark by EM-13 with the switch retained. For `SYSTEM` origin the structural check reads `GraphView.node_state(id)` and `section_dormant(section_id)` and never `served_pm` (a FAILED or DESTROYED node, or a live node on a dead bus, **accepts**). The GDD's per-node-state table (AC-33) is the test matrix and is not restated.

**D3.4 Mutators (E1..E10): a published object, scope first, three result shapes.** `EmitterMutators` is the published mutator object other owners receive through their `setup()` (the composition root wires it, ADR-0003 section 7). Every mutator begins with `scope.open_for(&"emitter.state")` and returns `REFUSED` without writing on a refused scope (counted `WRITE_OUTSIDE_SCOPE` by the kernel). Dirty keys are marked explicitly after the writes (D13.3). All mutators may be called from a HOOK or APPLY scope (any block writable, ADR-0003 section 4) or from the INIT scope (E1, E10, E4, E9 from Web Map's `init_world` and the new-game step).

| # | Mutator | Class | Signature (all begin `scope: WriteScope`) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | `instantiate_section_emitters` | A | `(scope, section_id, out: EmitterOutcome) -> int`, with pure `check_instantiate(views, section_id) -> StringName` | creates fixtures, lanterns and the beacon from the section template's emitter placements and the Item DB `emits` defs; reads no other block's state (`pod_at` included); `node_ref = node_base(section_id) + node_ordinal` (ADR-0013 section 3); an authored-on Graph-powered lamp is created ARMING with M14 queued and `arm_tick` from D5.2 at `T_a` = the creation tick; a self-powered EMERGENCY authored on is created ON; a DOCK_STATUS glow is created OFF whatever the authoring says; creations are admitted in `priority` order at the cap (D12.5) |
| E2 | `discard_section_emitters` | A | `(scope, section_id, out) -> int` | removes the section's emitters (deployables included), unregisters the section's OBJECT subjects, drops pair rows and grid entries; no MVP caller |
| E3 | `spawn_deployable` | B | `(scope, kind, pos_x, pos_y, owner, life_ticks, out: EmitterOutcome) -> void` | `out.code` is `OK`, `REFUSED_CAP` or `NO_SECTION` (dormant, unloaded or unknown section); resolves the section from the landing position with `LayoutView.section_at`, converts once to section-local px; over `MAX_DEPLOYABLES_LIVE` puts the lowest-id non-evicting stick of the same kind into the visible evict-wane (never an instant removal); `life_ticks` is the life remaining at landing |
| E4 | `bind_beam` | A | `(scope, player_id, shape_id, out) -> int` | once at new game; the only way a beam's shape changes |
| E5 | `force_off` | B | `(scope, beam_id) -> void` | sets `switch_on` false; neither reads nor writes `last_toggle_tick` |
| E6 | `register_subject` | B | `(scope, ref, kind, anchor_x, anchor_y, section_id, out) -> void` | `out.code`: `OK`, `DUPLICATE` (idempotent, **not** a defect: TR-horror-039), `OVER_CAP` (`emitter_subjects_overflow`), `OVER_MOVING_CAP` (`emitter_moving_overflow`), `NO_SECTION`; D2.5 pending rules |
| E7 | `unregister_subject` | B | `(scope, ref) -> void` | pending-unregister |
| E8 | `set_subject_anchor` | B | `(scope, ref, anchor_x, anchor_y) -> void` | pending anchor; lands at the next run |
| E9 | `create_seat_beam` | A | `(scope, player_id, out) -> int` | allocates the id from the block counter, sets `last_toggle_tick` to -1, returns the id in `out.id`; the kernel binds it from `beam_bindings()` (D3.5) |
| E10 | `set_dock_status` | A (infallible apply) | `(scope, section_id, on, out) -> int` | self-powered: no M14, no ARMING, no commit-spacing guard, no `last_toggle_tick` write; recomputes that record's `output_pm`, `lit`, `r_lit_px`, `r_off_px` at once so the glow is complete from P4 of the same tick; an unknown section or no DOCK_STATUS glow changes nothing, returns `OK`, sets `out.code = NO_DOCK_GLOW` and increments `emitter_dock_status_missing` (a lint-prevented defect must not fault the caller's whole apply) |

`EmitterOutcome` (`src/sim/emitter/emitter_outcome.gd`, `RefCounted`, caller-owned and reused): `code: int`, `id: int`, `count: int`. A Class B mutator keeps `-> void` and clamps, never rejects, never calls `scope.fault`; an unknown id is a no-op that sets `out.code`. Callers hold one outcome object per call site, so a call allocates nothing.

**D3.5 Binding source (TR-emitter-009).** `binding_source(ctx)` is the descriptor field and `ctx.put`s a flat `PackedInt64Array` `[player_id, beam_id, ...]` in **ascending `player_id`**, even length, built from the beam rows (`kind == BEAM`, `owner_ref` the PlayerId) into a pre-sized scratch array and duplicated for the `put` (ADR-0016 sections 6.1 and 6.2; the GDD's `[(player_id, beam_id)]` list becomes this flat array, a GDD sync item). `toggle_beam` carries `OWNED_BY_ISSUER` with source `emitter.state`, and the first tick of a restored run passes the authority check because the kernel's LOADING rebuild binds from this source after every `post_restore` (ADR-0016 KRN-RST-06).

**D4.1 Eight steps, fixed order, one pass each.** `emitter.place` does exactly the following, in this order, and nothing else; each step is a bounded loop over a count or a literal (no iterate-to-convergence, no recursion, no catch-up):

## @hot
static func in_cone(rx: int, ry: int, d2: int, ux: int, uy: int, cos2_q28: int) -> bool:
	if d2 == 0:

	var dd: int = rx * ux + ry * uy       # Q14 dot product

The `dd > 0` guard is required (the squared test alone accepts the opposite half-plane); a 360-degree shape (`OMNI`) skips the call. **BEAM_SPLIT is the OR of two such tests** at axes `aim +- split_axis_units` (both axes are posmod-wrapped); the dark wedge never closes (I-WEDGE), so a point lies in at most one cone and its contribution is never doubled. `cos2_q28` is the squared Q14 cosine of `half_angle_units` derived by the catalog freeze (D1.2). **Mirror exactness is a test, not a hope:** exposure of a mirrored scene (x to -x, aim `a` to `AIM_UNITS/2 - a`, `flip_h` toggled) equals the mirror image of the original exactly, for the five drawn and three mirrored facings, every `CHEST_POINT` animation row and all four beam shapes. No float, trig or square root is on the path. Magnitudes: `|r| <= REACH_MAX_PX + CHEST_X_MAX`, `|dd| <= |r| * 16384`, `dd * dd` and `d2 * cos2_q28` stay below 2^62 by a wide margin (the product bound of the registry reach range is about 4 x 10^13); `I-OVERFLOW` proves it at boot for the declared constants, not for a hand-picked case.

**D7.2 Quantisation.** The direction table is Q14 and the half-angles and the split offset are not integral in `AIM_UNITS`, so the rim is misplaced by under 0.1 degree (under 0.7 px at the longest reach); the quantisation sits far inside the accepted committed-versus-drawn divergence (PC-5 tolerance) and is the same on the sim and drawn sides because Lighting derives its cone from the same `ShapeCatalog` rows (a build lint, TR-emitter-016: the rendered reach of every hard-edged row equals the table reach within one pixel). Probed 2026-10-29: the generated table has 0 mirror mismatches over all 4,096 entries; the squared length of an entry deviates from 2^28 by at most 22,314 (a relative length error below 5 x 10^-5, under 0.02 px at the longest reach); the five `cos2_q28` values derived from it equal the GDD's EM-8 column exactly.

### 8. The integer occlusion test (TR-emitter-018, -044; Emitter candidate 1)

**D8.1 Source.** Occlusion is an integer segment-versus-rectangle test over the OCCLUDES_LIGHT rectangles of one body, obtained through the `OccluderSource` port of ADR-0014 and **nothing else**: no physics backend, no direct-space-state query, no rendering occluder (Alternative 1). Actors and horrors never occlude (they are not rectangles). Door state is the Layout projection of the Graph's `door_state` (the leaf rectangle is already in the OCCLUDES_LIGHT set at its current extent, ADR-0014 section 1), so the Emitter holds **no door flag** and no open-fraction threshold exists. One `QueryBuffer` is owned by `EmitterScratch`, sized at the freeze to its worst result (`MAX_FOOTPRINT_RECTS_PER_BODY`, ADR-0014 section 4), and reused for every pair; `out.grew` stays 0 after warm-up (a test asserts it).

**D8.2 Box convention (the cell-unit rule, GDD EM-20 a).** Layout's coordinates name pixel cells; a cell is the unit square centred on its integer coordinate. `rects_in` returns the occupied span `(x0, y0, x1 - 1, y1 - 1)` of each rectangle in `out.spans`; the box tested is the **closed** continuous box `[x0 - 1/2, (x1 - 1) + 1/2] x [y0 - 1/2, (y1 - 1) + 1/2]`, computed in **doubled coordinates** as the integer box `[2*x0 - 1, 2*(x1-1) + 1] x [2*y0 - 1, 2*(y1-1) + 1]` (equivalently `[2*x0 - 1, 2*x1 - 1]` in the stored half-open terms). Abutting rectangles share a box face, so no wall seam, door-leaf/jamb joint or corner join leaves a strip; a touch (corner graze, edge-on pass) is blocked; a segment endpoint is an integer cell, doubled to an even number against odd box bounds, so it is never exactly on a box face and is inside a box iff its cell is occupied. The candidate query box is the segment's cell bounding box, half-open: `ax0 = min(sx, px)`, `ax1 = max(sx, px) + 1`, likewise y. **This is exactly the set of rectangles whose closed box can touch the segment** (a rectangle's box meets the segment's doubled bounding box iff `x0 <= maxx` and `x1 > minx`, which is the half-open overlap `rects_in` computes), so the broadphase neither misses a blocker nor the doubled test needs a second filter.

**D8.3 Test (slab method on integers, no division).** `SegmentMath.blocked(sx, sy, px, py, spans, count) -> bool` translates every coordinate relative to `S` and doubles it, then for each box clips the parameter interval `[t_lo, t_hi]` (initially `[0, 1]`) against each axis slab by **cross-multiplication of fractions with positive denominators**; the box blocks iff `t_lo <= t_hi` at the end (closed). An axis with zero extent is `outside` (no hit) when `S'` lies outside the slab and unbounded otherwise.

```gdscript
## @hot   spans: QueryBuffer.spans (4 ints per record: x0, y0, x1-1, y1-1), count: QueryBuffer.count
static func blocked(sx: int, sy: int, px: int, py: int, spans: PackedInt32Array, count: int) -> bool:
	var dx: int = (px - sx) * 2
	var dy: int = (py - sy) * 2
	for i in range(count):
		var b: int = i * 4
		var x0: int = (spans[b] - sx) * 2 - 1           # box in doubled coordinates, relative to S (S' = 0)
		var y0: int = (spans[b + 1] - sy) * 2 - 1
		var x1: int = (spans[b + 2] - sx) * 2 + 1
		var y1: int = (spans[b + 3] - sy) * 2 + 1
		var ln: int = 0                                  # t_lo = ln / ld   (ld > 0)
		var ld: int = 1
		var hn: int = 1                                  # t_hi = hn / hd   (hd > 0)
		var hd: int = 1
		var hit: bool = true
		# x slab
		if dx == 0:
			hit = x0 <= 0 and 0 <= x1
		else:
			var en: int = x0 if dx > 0 else -x1          # entry numerator (denominator |dx|)
			var ex: int = x1 if dx > 0 else -x0
			var den: int = dx if dx > 0 else -dx
			if en * ld > ln * den:
				ln = en
				ld = den
			if ex * hd < hn * den:
				hn = ex
				hd = den
		# y slab (same shape) ... then: hit = hit and ln * hd <= hn * ld
		if hit and _y_slab_and_test(y0, y1, dy, ln, ld, hn, hd):
			return true
	return false
```

(The listing shows the shape; the y slab is the same code with `y0/y1/dy`, and the final comparison is `ln * hd <= hn * ld`. A helper is permitted inside a `@hot` function as long as it is itself tagged. The implementation story writes both axes inline.) Every value is an integer relative to `S`; with `I-BOUNDS` (body-frame coordinates below `BODY_COORD_LIMIT`, an ADR-0015 bounds-ledger assumption) the doubled relative values are below 2^26, so every cross product is below 2^52, well inside `I-OVERFLOW`. **Probed 2026-10-29:** 300,000 random segment/box cases (24,519 blocked, including touches) produced **0 mismatches** against an independent separating-axis implementation (bounding-box overlap plus corner-side signs, exact integers), and the GDD's oblique seam-leak example (rectangles `[0,24)` and `[24,48)`, segment `(23,300)` to `(24,140)`) is blocked.

**D8.4 Anchor clearance (TR-emitter-044).** An anchor is at least `ANCHOR_CLEARANCE_PX` outside every occluding rectangle (Chebyshev distance in cells from the occupied span, ADR-0013 `rect_algebra_closed_span`). It is a **data-load lint** `EMITTER_ANCHOR_CLEARANCE` over every authored FIXTURE, NODE_LANTERN and BEACON placement and every subject anchor the content can declare (the lint uses `ExposureProbe` and `section_rects_into`, D1.1) and a creation-time check for FAULT_GLOW anchors. At run time an anchor found strictly inside a footprint is **treated as blocked from every emitter** (`lux` 0, `lit` false, fails safe to dark), **still counts in `section_emission`** (an emitter anchored in its wall lights nothing but is still emission), and increments the per-record counter `emitter_anchor_clearance_fail`. The runtime check is one `solid`-free test: an anchor cell inside any returned span is "inside" (a zero-length segment test, `S == P`, which the same function answers).

**D8.5 Hard parts handled once, here.** (a) A zero-length segment (`d2 == 0`, the subject at the emitter's occlusion origin) is answered by the same function (both axes zero-extent). (b) The owner's own beam on the owner's ACTOR subject contributes its apex value with no cone and no occlusion test (D9.4). (c) The segment test is called only for pairs that survived the radius and cone rejects; the call count and the rectangle count are the `W_SEG`/`K_OCC` units of D12.

### 9. Illumination and the lit hysteresis (TR-emitter-019, -020; Emitter candidate 3)

**D9.1 Contribution.** For one emitter and one subject `c` is 0 unless all hold: equal `body_id`, `d2 <= reach_px^2` (closed), inside the cone for cone shapes, unblocked. Otherwise `Illumination.contribution(output_pm, curve_class, edge_floor_pm, d, reach) -> int`: `F = IntMath.floor_div(1000 * (reach - d), reach)`; SOFT `f = F`; HARD `f = edge_floor_pm + IntMath.floor_div((1000 - edge_floor_pm) * F, 1000)`; `c = IntMath.floor_div(output_pm * f, 1000)`, with `d = max{k : SQ[k] <= d2}` (D1.4). All operands are non-negative (`d <= reach`), so `floor_div` is exact; `reach >= REACH_MIN_PX > 0` (I-REACH), so no division by zero occurs. Curve classes are rows of `ShapeCatalog` (`LINEAR` is the MVP curve id; a replacement 17-knot interpolation table keeps the signature and must be monotone, integer and non-negative).

**D9.2 Aggregation.** `lux_pm = mini(1000, Sum c)` over every emitter, `act_lux_pm = mini(1000, Sum c)` over emitters whose `gates_actions` is true (the BEACON does not gate, so it adds to `lux` and not to `act_lux`), with **no ambient term** (`AMBIENT_PM` is fixed at 0 in the sim). Integer addition is commutative, so the sum is independent of candidate order. `top_emitter_id` is the emitter of the largest contribution, ties by **ascending id**, an explicit comparison and not an iteration-order accident.

**D9.3 Published radii.** `r_lit_px` and `r_off_px` are the largest `d` in `0..reach` whose integer chain gives `c >= LIT_ON_PM` and `c >= LIT_OFF_PM` respectively (-1 when `c(0)` is below the threshold), found by binary search because `c` is monotone non-increasing in `d`; the second search is bounded to the window above `r_lit_px` (`Illumination.radius_for`). The closed form `floor(R * (output - LIT_ON_PM) / output)` runs 1 px high for some dimmed outputs and is not used. They are derived on an output or reach change and in `post_restore`, never persisted. For a full-output hard-edged emitter the lit boundary **is** the drawn edge (invariant I-EDGE); a dimmed one has an honestly smaller actionable area.

**D9.4 The owner stands in their own light (EM-21).** The owner's own beam adds its full `output_pm` (the `d = 0` apex value, which every cone contains) to the owner's ACTOR `lux_pm`, independent of facing and occlusion; it is **not** added to `act_lux_pm`; every other beam lights the owner, and the owner's beam lights everyone else, by the ordinary tests. Attention reads the beam as emission and does not add it again.

**D9.5 Lit hysteresis (decided; the "lit hysteresis" of the task scope).** `LitHysteresis.next(prev, act_lux_pm, on_pm, off_pm) -> int` is `1` iff `act_lux_pm >= LIT_ON_PM`, or `prev == 1` and `act_lux_pm >= LIT_OFF_PM`; there is **no dwell** (`LIT_OFF_DWELL_TICKS` is fixed at 0: holding `lit` after the light is gone would be a window where the sim says lit and the world is dark, a P1 lie). Decisions: (a) **the bit is canonical**, one `PackedByteArray` entry per subject, snapshotted and hashed (EM-22, checkpoint ruling CP-2): a subject saved at 130 permille and lit is lit after the restore, and rebuilding every bit against `LIT_ON_PM` is rejected because `validate` at T+1 would accept in one run and reject `NOT_LIT` in the other; (b) `post_restore` recomputes `lux_pm`, `act_lux_pm` and `top_emitter_id` from the restored state and **keeps the bit**; applying `next` again in the same state is **idempotent** (a fixed `act` cannot flip a bit it just produced), which is what lets the cold build run the same W6 as the live run; (c) a hard rim is a step (a full-output rim contributes `EDGE_FLOOR_PM` then 0 across one pixel) that the hysteresis never sees, so it bites only for dimmed or soft light (brownout, waning sticks, fixture pools); rim chatter under a sweeping beam is the Controller's committed-aim quantisation and `FOCUS_STICKY_MARGIN` (PC-6); (d) `lit(ref)` and `lux(ref)` stay separate answers (the beacon must not strobe prompts, EM-16); (e) a newly registered subject starts unlit and is evaluated at the next run; (f) an unregistered ref answers `lux` 0 and `lit` false in a release build, indistinguishable from an unlit registered one (no existence oracle; the debug-only `registered(ref)` is for tests and the overlay). The two `lit`s keep their GDD names verbatim: the record field `lit` (`output_pm > 0`, the beam draws only when it is true) and the query `lit(ref)`.

**D9.6 What the kernel is not.** It is not `probe(body_id, point)` or `lit_by` (deferred to VS-A, banned by lint `EMT-06`), not a shadow or light renderer (Lighting conforms to the published fields), and it never takes a Filter-wrapped value.

### 4. The hook: order of work, and nothing pending past the tick (TR-emitter-002, -021, -022, -025, -037, TR-interact-038)

**D4.1 Eight steps, fixed order, one pass each.** `emitter.place` does exactly the following, in this order, and nothing else; each step is a bounded loop over a count or a literal (no iterate-to-convergence, no recursion, no catch-up):

| Step | Work | Reads | Writes (derived unless marked) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **W0** read upstream; frames | per section in the section cache (ascending `section_id`): compare the version triple (D11.4); on a `static_version` change re-read `body_of` and `section_offset_x/_y` and rewrite the derived `body_id`/offset of every record and non-ACTOR subject of that section (cost `W_FRAME` each); per bound beam and ACTOR subject: `BodyView.actor_of_seat`, `actor_section`, `body_of_actor` (a foot that crosses a door moves the beam's section in that tick; `actor_section` 0 keeps the previous value and counts `emitter_actor_section_none`); `GraphView.last_step_no()` for the fault-glow gate | Layout, `OccluderSource`, Body, Graph | section cache, derived `body_id`, ACTOR `section_id`/anchor |
| **W1** lifecycle | DEAD force-off (a read of `ControllerView.loco_state`, no command); deployable aging and evict-wane progress and removal; arming (`T >= arm_tick` realises an ON and writes **canonical** `last_toggle_tick = arm_tick`, D3.7); FAULT_GLOW reconcile once per completed Graph step (D6.4) | Controller, Graph | **canonical:** `switch_on` (DEAD), `life_remaining_ticks`, `last_toggle_tick`, FAULT_GLOW rows, `fault_step_seen`; row removals |
| **W2** derive | every emitter in ascending id: `origin`, `aim`, `half_angle_units`, `reach_px`, `output_pm`, record `lit`, `r_lit_px`/`r_off_px` (only when `output_pm` or `reach_px` changed and stays above zero; an output of 0 sets both to -1 with no search), the per-section emission term | Graph (`served_pm`, `run_pm`, `node_state`), Controller, Body | record derived fields, `emission[]` |
| **W3** find changes | apply every `pending` row (D2.5); list the static rows whose inputs changed: output or integer reach change, create, remove, resting-subject register, move or unregister, occluder region (D11.3), frame change (D11.5), cold; bump `static_epoch` (D11.6) if anything static changed | W2 results, section cache | `pending` cleared (**canonical**), change lists in scratch |
| **W4** deltas, synchronous | update the pair rows and raw sums by delta in ascending (emitter id, subject ref); **nothing is left pending past W4** | change lists | pair rows, raw sums |
| **W5** dynamic layer | for each dynamic item (beam cone(s), beam foot spill, beacon cone) in ascending emitter id: candidates from the subject grids, then radius, then cone, then occlusion (cheapest first); movers' static sweep (D11.6) | grids, `OccluderSource` | scratch sums |
| **W6** sums, hysteresis, commit | per subject in ascending ref: `lux_pm`, `act_lux_pm`, `top_emitter_id`, `lit` bit (canonical write), `last_eval_tick`; `hdr.last_place_tick = T` | scratch, pair rows | subject table, **canonical** `lit`, `last_place_tick` |
| **W7** publish | dirty keys (D13.3); the per-section emission array becomes current; the units tally closes (D12.3) | derived | keys, `emission[]`, `EmitterDiag` |

The static layer's contract is **never stale and synchronous** (EM-23): W3 and W4 finish every update inside the tick, before W6 writes the table, so the staleness bound of D.13 (age 0 for a reader `after: [emitter.place]`, age 1 for P2 `validate`, a render-rate poll and a hook ordered earlier) holds for every reader; a tick whose updates exceed the ceiling still completes them and counts `emitter_rebuild_over_ceiling` (D12.4). GDD alternative (b), a counted-unit cap with a deferral queue, is rejected for the same reasons as in EM-23: it would make `lit` depend on a derived queue that a restore (which rebuilds cold and complete) cannot reproduce.

**D4.2 No snapshot copy (decided; revises the mechanism of TR-emitter-025, not its intent).** EM-25 specifies a per-tick snapshot "built once in W7" so that readers see stable columns. This ADR does not build one. The subject table and the emitter derived columns are written **only inside `emitter.place`** (and by a creation mutator for its own new row, D2.5); the kernel is single-threaded and the presentation stages run between ticks (ADR-0009), so any read outside `emitter.place` already sees a committed table, and no reader runs *inside* the hook. A copy would cost `W_SNAP` units per emitter every tick (D.14 prices it at about 4 % of `B` at the typical point) to protect against a race that cannot occur. What TR-emitter-025 asks for survives: reads are pure table lookups (typed scalar getters over packed columns, ascending id by construction), at most one tick stale unless the reader declares `after: [emitter.place]`, allocation-free, never callable from a notification handler that decides state, with the no-retain rule kept for list reads (they fill a caller-owned buffer, D13.1). `T_snap` leaves the budget model; the per-section emission array of D.12 is accumulated in W2 and made current in W7, and a late-created (`pending`) emitter is absent from it until the next run, the same one-tick lag as the subject table.

### 5. Output derivations (TR-emitter-013, -014, -015, -016, -029, TR-itemdb-034)

**D5.1 Lamp output (TR-emitter-014).** `LampMath.lamp_output(base_pm, served_pm, switch_on, armed, live) -> int` is `IntMath.floor_div(base_pm * served_pm, 1000)` when `switch_on`, `armed` and `live` hold, else 0. `served_pm` is the tier's satisfaction read live each run from `GraphView.served_pm(node_id)` (ADR-0011 section 9.1; persisted as `n_served` per ADR-0012, so it is exact straight after a restore); the Emitter's own `switch_on` gates the light (a switched-off lamp can still read `served_pm` 1000). A lamp is **live** iff its node exists in the Graph read view, is not dormant (`section_dormant`) or tombstoned, and `node_state` is not FAILED, DESTROYED, SALVAGED or ABSENT (EM-13). A not-live lamp keeps `switch_on` and relights on repair with no command. A node with `node_ref` 0 (the two self-powered subkinds) has no liveness test, no ARMING and a fixed `base_pm`.

**D5.2 Arming latency (TR-emitter-013).** `arm_tick` is the first tick at or after the apply tick `T_a` on which a power hook runs: `arm_tick = T_a + IntMath.posmod_i(power_offset - T_a, GRAPH_STEP_TICKS)`, with `power_offset` and `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` read from the frozen `GraphTuning` catalog injected at `setup()` (ADR-0012 makes the hook offsets tuning data, so the GDD's `T_a mod GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` form, which assumes offset 0, is generalised; at offset 0 the two are identical, which is a unit test). This agrees with ADR-0012's drain rule (a P2 apply on a power-hook tick is drained by the same tick's phase 0; an apply on any other tick by the next power-hook tick), so a lamp is ARMING with output 0 for 0 to `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS - 1` ticks and is lit by the first `emitter.place` at or after `arm_tick`. OFF is immediate with M14 `(node_ref, 0)`. M14 is called **inside the apply** through the injected Graph mutator object (`views` cannot write; the Graph's published mutators are wired by the composition root, ADR-0003 section 7). An M14 deposited under the INIT scope (E1 at `init_world`) is drained at the first power hook (ADR-0012 section 5, assumption). The negative case of D.2 (a Graph that consumes only strictly later requests) is a `GraphTuning` fact the unit tests parameterise, not a second code path.

**D6.3 Cap on records (TR-emitter-023 part).** At `MAX_EMITTERS` a creation is **refused**, never made by removing a light with a physical cause (D12.5).

**D6.4 Fault glow: derived, reconciled once per completed Graph step, never in `post_restore` (TR-emitter-027, TR-ftrail-041; answers ADR-0012 Open Question 3).** FAULT_GLOW rows are canonical (they carry `glow_key`, `sev`, `placed_tick`), so a restore restores them; they are created and removed by W1 and by nothing else. W1 reconciles **iff `GraphView.last_step_no() != hdr.fault_step_seen`**, that is, once for each Graph step the failure hook has completed, on the tick after its phase 11 ran (the hook is `after: graph.propagate.failure`, so it reads that step's final descriptor store), and then writes `fault_step_seen = last_step_no`. `post_restore` does not reconcile and does not touch the rows. Consequences: in the uninterrupted run and in the restored run the reconciliation happens at the same ticks against a descriptor store freshly produced by the same phase 11, so the one-step window ADR-0012 section 11 leaves in the *store* between a restore and the next phase 11 is never read by the Emitter; the glow of a descriptor appears on the failure tick of the step in which it appears, never later (EM-1). Reconciliation reads `GraphView.failures(filter, out)` with a reusable `FailureFilter` (`loaded_only`, `min_sev` from the glow table) and compares it, in ascending descriptor id, with the existing FAULT_GLOW rows keyed by `glow_key`: new descriptors with a glow row (`GlowTable`, keyed by `(mode, medium)`) create a row, vanished ones remove it, `sev` changes update `sev` (and the derived output `IntMath.floor_div(GLOW_BASE_PM[key] * SEV_GLOW_PM[sev], 1000)`), subject to `sev >= sev_min[key]` and output above zero. Position, section and frame: `section_id = GraphView.section_of(anchor)`, `anchor_px` = the head point `base_px_polyline[0]` of `LayoutView.anchor_geometry(anchor)` read once at creation (a cold read; an empty answer for a discarded section creates no row, counts `emitter_fault_glow_no_anchor` and retries at the next step), and `body_id` derived. Cap: `MAX_FAULT_GLOW`; beyond it the evicted rows are the unprotected ones of lowest `sev`, ties by the higher descriptor id first, and a row younger than `ticks_for_seconds(W_MIN_WARNING_S)` (age `T - placed_tick`) is protected and never evicted: protection beats the cap (`emitter_fault_glow_overcap`, `emitter_fault_glow_evictions`). The trail's emissive layer adds nothing to exposure (a FAULT_GLOW is the only fault light the sim knows). The Failure & Trail glow table is stage-1 content (`GlowTable`), authored by Failure & Trail, read here as data (architecture IC-12).

### 7. The integer cone test (TR-emitter-017; Emitter candidate 3)

**D7.1 Test.** `ConeMath.in_cone(rx, ry, d2, ux, uy, cos2_q28) -> bool` where `r = anchor - origin` (body frame), `d2 = rx*rx + ry*ry` (the caller has already established `d2 <= reach * reach`, a closed edge), `(ux, uy)` is the Q14 axis `DirTable.UX/UY[IntMath.posmod_i(aim + off, AIM_UNITS)]`:

```gdscript
## @hot
static func in_cone(rx: int, ry: int, d2: int, ux: int, uy: int, cos2_q28: int) -> bool:
	if d2 == 0:
		return true                       # the apex is inside every cone of its emitter
	var dd: int = rx * ux + ry * uy       # Q14 dot product
	return dd > 0 and dd * dd >= d2 * cos2_q28
```

The `dd > 0` guard is required (the squared test alone accepts the opposite half-plane); a 360-degree shape (`OMNI`) skips the call. **BEAM_SPLIT is the OR of two such tests** at axes `aim +- split_axis_units` (both axes are posmod-wrapped); the dark wedge never closes (I-WEDGE), so a point lies in at most one cone and its contribution is never doubled. `cos2_q28` is the squared Q14 cosine of `half_angle_units` derived by the catalog freeze (D1.2). **Mirror exactness is a test, not a hope:** exposure of a mirrored scene (x to -x, aim `a` to `AIM_UNITS/2 - a`, `flip_h` toggled) equals the mirror image of the original exactly, for the five drawn and three mirrored facings, every `CHEST_POINT` animation row and all four beam shapes. No float, trig or square root is on the path. Magnitudes: `|r| <= REACH_MAX_PX + CHEST_X_MAX`, `|dd| <= |r| * 16384`, `dd * dd` and `d2 * cos2_q28` stay below 2^62 by a wide margin (the product bound of the registry reach range is about 4 x 10^13); `I-OVERFLOW` proves it at boot for the declared constants, not for a hand-picked case.

**D7.2 Quantisation.** The direction table is Q14 and the half-angles and the split offset are not integral in `AIM_UNITS`, so the rim is misplaced by under 0.1 degree (under 0.7 px at the longest reach); the quantisation sits far inside the accepted committed-versus-drawn divergence (PC-5 tolerance) and is the same on the sim and drawn sides because Lighting derives its cone from the same `ShapeCatalog` rows (a build lint, TR-emitter-016: the rendered reach of every hard-edged row equals the table reach within one pixel). Probed 2026-10-29: the generated table has 0 mirror mismatches over all 4,096 entries; the squared length of an entry deviates from 2^28 by at most 22,314 (a relative length error below 5 x 10^-5, under 0.02 px at the longest reach); the five `cos2_q28` values derived from it equal the GDD's EM-8 column exactly.

### 8. The integer occlusion test (TR-emitter-018, -044; Emitter candidate 1)

**D8.1 Source.** Occlusion is an integer segment-versus-rectangle test over the OCCLUDES_LIGHT rectangles of one body, obtained through the `OccluderSource` port of ADR-0014 and **nothing else**: no physics backend, no direct-space-state query, no rendering occluder (Alternative 1). Actors and horrors never occlude (they are not rectangles). Door state is the Layout projection of the Graph's `door_state` (the leaf rectangle is already in the OCCLUDES_LIGHT set at its current extent, ADR-0014 section 1), so the Emitter holds **no door flag** and no open-fraction threshold exists. One `QueryBuffer` is owned by `EmitterScratch`, sized at the freeze to its worst result (`MAX_FOOTPRINT_RECTS_PER_BODY`, ADR-0014 section 4), and reused for every pair; `out.grew` stays 0 after warm-up (a test asserts it).

**D8.2 Box convention (the cell-unit rule, GDD EM-20 a).** Layout's coordinates name pixel cells; a cell is the unit square centred on its integer coordinate. `rects_in` returns the occupied span `(x0, y0, x1 - 1, y1 - 1)` of each rectangle in `out.spans`; the box tested is the **closed** continuous box `[x0 - 1/2, (x1 - 1) + 1/2] x [y0 - 1/2, (y1 - 1) + 1/2]`, computed in **doubled coordinates** as the integer box `[2*x0 - 1, 2*(x1-1) + 1] x [2*y0 - 1, 2*(y1-1) + 1]` (equivalently `[2*x0 - 1, 2*x1 - 1]` in the stored half-open terms). Abutting rectangles share a box face, so no wall seam, door-leaf/jamb joint or corner join leaves a strip; a touch (corner graze, edge-on pass) is blocked; a segment endpoint is an integer cell, doubled to an even number against odd box bounds, so it is never exactly on a box face and is inside a box iff its cell is occupied. The candidate query box is the segment's cell bounding box, half-open: `ax0 = min(sx, px)`, `ax1 = max(sx, px) + 1`, likewise y. **This is exactly the set of rectangles whose closed box can touch the segment** (a rectangle's box meets the segment's doubled bounding box iff `x0 <= maxx` and `x1 > minx`, which is the half-open overlap `rects_in` computes), so the broadphase neither misses a blocker nor the doubled test needs a second filter.

**D8.3 Test (slab method on integers, no division).** `SegmentMath.blocked(sx, sy, px, py, spans, count) -> bool` translates every coordinate relative to `S` and doubles it, then for each box clips the parameter interval `[t_lo, t_hi]` (initially `[0, 1]`) against each axis slab by **cross-multiplication of fractions with positive denominators**; the box blocks iff `t_lo <= t_hi` at the end (closed). An axis with zero extent is `outside` (no hit) when `S'` lies outside the slab and unbounded otherwise.

```gdscript
## @hot   spans: QueryBuffer.spans (4 ints per record: x0, y0, x1-1, y1-1), count: QueryBuffer.count
static func blocked(sx: int, sy: int, px: int, py: int, spans: PackedInt32Array, count: int) -> bool:
	var dx: int = (px - sx) * 2
	var dy: int = (py - sy) * 2
	for i in range(count):
		var b: int = i * 4
		var x0: int = (spans[b] - sx) * 2 - 1           # box in doubled coordinates, relative to S (S' = 0)
		var y0: int = (spans[b + 1] - sy) * 2 - 1
		var x1: int = (spans[b + 2] - sx) * 2 + 1
		var y1: int = (spans[b + 3] - sy) * 2 + 1
		var ln: int = 0                                  # t_lo = ln / ld   (ld > 0)
		var ld: int = 1
		var hn: int = 1                                  # t_hi = hn / hd   (hd > 0)
		var hd: int = 1
		var hit: bool = true
		# x slab
		if dx == 0:
			hit = x0 <= 0 and 0 <= x1
		else:
			var en: int = x0 if dx > 0 else -x1          # entry numerator (denominator |dx|)
			var ex: int = x1 if dx > 0 else -x0
			var den: int = dx if dx > 0 else -dx
			if en * ld > ln * den:
				ln = en
				ld = den
			if ex * hd < hn * den:
				hn = ex
				hd = den
		# y slab (same shape) ... then: hit = hit and ln * hd <= hn * ld
		if hit and _y_slab_and_test(y0, y1, dy, ln, ld, hn, hd):
			return true
	return false
```

(The listing shows the shape; the y slab is the same code with `y0/y1/dy`, and the final comparison is `ln * hd <= hn * ld`. A helper is permitted inside a `@hot` function as long as it is itself tagged. The implementation story writes both axes inline.) Every value is an integer relative to `S`; with `I-BOUNDS` (body-frame coordinates below `BODY_COORD_LIMIT`, an ADR-0015 bounds-ledger assumption) the doubled relative values are below 2^26, so every cross product is below 2^52, well inside `I-OVERFLOW`. **Probed 2026-10-29:** 300,000 random segment/box cases (24,519 blocked, including touches) produced **0 mismatches** against an independent separating-axis implementation (bounding-box overlap plus corner-side signs, exact integers), and the GDD's oblique seam-leak example (rectangles `[0,24)` and `[24,48)`, segment `(23,300)` to `(24,140)`) is blocked.

**D8.4 Anchor clearance (TR-emitter-044).** An anchor is at least `ANCHOR_CLEARANCE_PX` outside every occluding rectangle (Chebyshev distance in cells from the occupied span, ADR-0013 `rect_algebra_closed_span`). It is a **data-load lint** `EMITTER_ANCHOR_CLEARANCE` over every authored FIXTURE, NODE_LANTERN and BEACON placement and every subject anchor the content can declare (the lint uses `ExposureProbe` and `section_rects_into`, D1.1) and a creation-time check for FAULT_GLOW anchors. At run time an anchor found strictly inside a footprint is **treated as blocked from every emitter** (`lux` 0, `lit` false, fails safe to dark), **still counts in `section_emission`** (an emitter anchored in its wall lights nothing but is still emission), and increments the per-record counter `emitter_anchor_clearance_fail`. The runtime check is one `solid`-free test: an anchor cell inside any returned span is "inside" (a zero-length segment test, `S == P`, which the same function answers).

**D8.5 Hard parts handled once, here.** (a) A zero-length segment (`d2 == 0`, the subject at the emitter's occlusion origin) is answered by the same function (both axes zero-extent). (b) The owner's own beam on the owner's ACTOR subject contributes its apex value with no cone and no occlusion test (D9.4). (c) The segment test is called only for pairs that survived the radius and cone rejects; the call count and the rectangle count are the `W_SEG`/`K_OCC` units of D12.

### 9. Illumination and the lit hysteresis (TR-emitter-019, -020; Emitter candidate 3)

**D9.1 Contribution.** For one emitter and one subject `c` is 0 unless all hold: equal `body_id`, `d2 <= reach_px^2` (closed), inside the cone for cone shapes, unblocked. Otherwise `Illumination.contribution(output_pm, curve_class, edge_floor_pm, d, reach) -> int`: `F = IntMath.floor_div(1000 * (reach - d), reach)`; SOFT `f = F`; HARD `f = edge_floor_pm + IntMath.floor_div((1000 - edge_floor_pm) * F, 1000)`; `c = IntMath.floor_div(output_pm * f, 1000)`, with `d = max{k : SQ[k] <= d2}` (D1.4). All operands are non-negative (`d <= reach`), so `floor_div` is exact; `reach >= REACH_MIN_PX > 0` (I-REACH), so no division by zero occurs. Curve classes are rows of `ShapeCatalog` (`LINEAR` is the MVP curve id; a replacement 17-knot interpolation table keeps the signature and must be monotone, integer and non-negative).

**D9.2 Aggregation.** `lux_pm = mini(1000, Sum c)` over every emitter, `act_lux_pm = mini(1000, Sum c)` over emitters whose `gates_actions` is true (the BEACON does not gate, so it adds to `lux` and not to `act_lux`), with **no ambient term** (`AMBIENT_PM` is fixed at 0 in the sim). Integer addition is commutative, so the sum is independent of candidate order. `top_emitter_id` is the emitter of the largest contribution, ties by **ascending id**, an explicit comparison and not an iteration-order accident.

**D9.3 Published radii.** `r_lit_px` and `r_off_px` are the largest `d` in `0..reach` whose integer chain gives `c >= LIT_ON_PM` and `c >= LIT_OFF_PM` respectively (-1 when `c(0)` is below the threshold), found by binary search because `c` is monotone non-increasing in `d`; the second search is bounded to the window above `r_lit_px` (`Illumination.radius_for`). The closed form `floor(R * (output - LIT_ON_PM) / output)` runs 1 px high for some dimmed outputs and is not used. They are derived on an output or reach change and in `post_restore`, never persisted. For a full-output hard-edged emitter the lit boundary **is** the drawn edge (invariant I-EDGE); a dimmed one has an honestly smaller actionable area.

**D9.4 The owner stands in their own light (EM-21).** The owner's own beam adds its full `output_pm` (the `d = 0` apex value, which every cone contains) to the owner's ACTOR `lux_pm`, independent of facing and occlusion; it is **not** added to `act_lux_pm`; every other beam lights the owner, and the owner's beam lights everyone else, by the ordinary tests. Attention reads the beam as emission and does not add it again.

**D9.5 Lit hysteresis (decided; the "lit hysteresis" of the task scope).** `LitHysteresis.next(prev, act_lux_pm, on_pm, off_pm) -> int` is `1` iff `act_lux_pm >= LIT_ON_PM`, or `prev == 1` and `act_lux_pm >= LIT_OFF_PM`; there is **no dwell** (`LIT_OFF_DWELL_TICKS` is fixed at 0: holding `lit` after the light is gone would be a window where the sim says lit and the world is dark, a P1 lie). Decisions: (a) **the bit is canonical**, one `PackedByteArray` entry per subject, snapshotted and hashed (EM-22, checkpoint ruling CP-2): a subject saved at 130 permille and lit is lit after the restore, and rebuilding every bit against `LIT_ON_PM` is rejected because `validate` at T+1 would accept in one run and reject `NOT_LIT` in the other; (b) `post_restore` recomputes `lux_pm`, `act_lux_pm` and `top_emitter_id` from the restored state and **keeps the bit**; applying `next` again in the same state is **idempotent** (a fixed `act` cannot flip a bit it just produced), which is what lets the cold build run the same W6 as the live run; (c) a hard rim is a step (a full-output rim contributes `EDGE_FLOOR_PM` then 0 across one pixel) that the hysteresis never sees, so it bites only for dimmed or soft light (brownout, waning sticks, fixture pools); rim chatter under a sweeping beam is the Controller's committed-aim quantisation and `FOCUS_STICKY_MARGIN` (PC-6); (d) `lit(ref)` and `lux(ref)` stay separate answers (the beacon must not strobe prompts, EM-16); (e) a newly registered subject starts unlit and is evaluated at the next run; (f) an unregistered ref answers `lux` 0 and `lit` false in a release build, indistinguishable from an unlit registered one (no existence oracle; the debug-only `registered(ref)` is for tests and the overlay). The two `lit`s keep their GDD names verbatim: the record field `lit` (`output_pm > 0`, the beam draws only when it is true) and the query `lit(ref)`.

**D9.6 What the kernel is not.** It is not `probe(body_id, point)` or `lit_by` (deferred to VS-A, banned by lint `EMT-06`), not a shadow or light renderer (Lighting conforms to the published fields), and it never takes a Filter-wrapped value.
